plaatje-native-life-1916: Native Life in South Africa by Solomon T. Plaatje is catalogued here in a 1916 edition drawn from the Internet Archive. The sample held for this entry, however, shows only the stamped library pages of one copy. That copy is kept at the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration in Mussoorie, India. Its accession marks and lending rules show on the pages. No pages of Plaatje's text appear in the sample. The book's contents therefore cannot be described from the evidence provided here.
plaw-114-116-2016:
Public Law 114-116, the Child Nicotine Poisoning Prevention Act of 2015, demands child-safe packs for liquid nicotine. The 114th Congress passed it in January 2016. Liquid nicotine is the fluid used in electronic cigarettes, and it can poison a small child who drinks it.

Any nicotine in a liquid nicotine container in commerce must be packed to the child-resistant standards in the federal rules. The rules reach containers sold, made for sale, spread in commerce, or brought into the United States, and they name the test method. The act adds a savings clause. Nothing in it trims the power of the Secretary of Health and Human Services to regulate nicotine products. That power rests on the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and the tobacco control law the act names.
plaw-114-117-2016:
Public Law 114-117 has a pointed short name: the Grants Oversight and New Efficiency Act, or the GONE Act. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. Its whole aim, in its own heading, is to close out expired grants, the federal awards that linger on the books long after their work ends.

Within 180 days, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget must tell each agency head to report to Congress and the Secretary. The report is due by the end of the first calendar year after the act. Each report lists every federal grant award the agency holds, with counts by age, by zero-dollar balance, and by unspent balance. It must state the hurdles that slow closeout, and for the agency's 30 oldest grants, say why each one is still open.
plaw-114-118-2016:
Public Law 114-118 revises the working powers of three District of Columbia justice bodies. Its full name is the District of Columbia Courts, Public Defender Service, and Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency Act of 2015. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016.

Section 2 gives the District of Columbia Courts a debt tool. A new clause lets the Executive Officer collect a debt from a court worker or former worker who was overpaid by error, or who owes the courts on any other ground. The sum may be taken in monthly installments or at set pay intervals, by deduction from the worker's current pay in fair amounts. The deduction may reach wages, salary, incentive pay, back pay, and lump sum leave pay.
plaw-114-119-2016:
Public Law 114-119 is the International Megan's Law, built to guard children from sex crime across borders. Its full title speaks of preventing child exploitation and other sexual crimes through advance notice of travel by registered sex offenders. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016.

The act's parts, per its contents, set up an Angel Watch Center and give the United States Marshals Service a notice role. Sections cover international travel by offenders, shared notice with other countries, and a unique passport marker for covered sex offenders. The findings open with Megan Nicole Kanka, age seven. She was abducted, sexually assaulted, and murdered in 1994 in New Jersey by a predator who lived across the street, a past her family did not know.
plaw-114-120-2016:
Public Law 114-120, the Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2015, allows Coast Guard spending for fiscal years 2016 and 2017. The 114th Congress passed it in February 2016. Title I holds the authorizations themselves and a set of matching amendments.

Title II works through the running of the service. Its sections cover the Vice Commandant and vice admirals, the Coast Guard forgiving debts owed to it, and reform of how it buys ships and gear. The list runs on to polar icebreakers, air station closures, mission performance measures, and communications. Member-focused clauses cover graduate schooling in maritime operations, career growth, boards that decide whether senior enlisted members stay on, member pay, and moving funds to give medical care.
plaw-114-121-2016:
Public Law 114-121, the Electrify Africa Act of 2015, sets a United States policy to spread electric power in sub-Saharan Africa. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. Its purpose is to back the work of African countries to widen access to power that people can afford and count on. Such access can open growth that takes in all, create jobs, and cut poverty.

The policy is to work with African governments, world lenders, regional bodies, cooperatives, and private firms. The named goals are bold: first-time power and power services for at least 50,000,000 people by 2020, in cities and the countryside alike. The act also urges at least 20,000 added megawatts of generating power by 2020, from a broad mix of energy choices, and backs public-private partnerships for sound power in urban areas.
plaw-114-122-2016:
Public Law 114-122, the North Korea Sanctions and Policy Enhancement Act of 2016, tightens the enforcement of sanctions against the Government of North Korea. The 114th Congress passed it in February 2016. Title I is about probes, banned conduct, and penalties.

Title I sections cover a statement of policy, probes, reporting duties, the naming of persons for sanctions, and the seizure of property. Title II aims at North Korean arms spread, human rights abuses, and illicit acts. It covers a finding on North Korea as a place of prime money laundering concern, steady enforcement of United Nations Security Council resolutions, and sanctions on arms spread and on buying. More clauses cover stronger inspection powers, travel sanctions, and travel advice for United States citizens.
plaw-114-123-2016:
Public Law 114-123, the United States-Jordan Defense Cooperation Act of 2015, deepens defense ties with the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. The findings set the scene. As of January 22, 2015, the United States had given more than three billion dollars in aid for the Syria crisis, nearly 467 million of it to Jordan.

The findings count 621,937 registered Syrian refugees in Jordan as of January 2015, most living outside camps. They recall the 2000 free-trade deal and Jordan's 1996 grant of major non-NATO ally status. Jordan faces the refugee strain and the threat of the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant, and its pilot Moaz al-Kasasbeh was murdered by that group. The act calls stronger defense ties a matter of United States security, on a par with the NATO allies and close partners it names.
plaw-114-124-2016:
Public Law 114-124 pairs a long name with a short one: the Research Excellence and Advancements for Dyslexia Act, or the READ Act. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It orders the National Science Foundation to do research on dyslexia, a reading disability. It also tells the Foundation to show the funding for its disabilities education program as its own line in the yearly budget request.

Congress finds that as many as one in six American school children, about 8,500,000, may have dyslexia. It notes dyslexia has counted as a learning disability under federal education law since 1975. The act leaves the Foundation's Research in Disabilities Education program as it is, and tells it to keep backing work on how disabilities shape learning in science, technology, engineering, and math. A dyslexia section then calls for research across the Foundation's branches, won through open, merit-based contests.
plaw-114-125-2016:
Public Law 114-125, the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015, reauthorizes the customs work of easing trade and policing it. The 114th Congress passed it in February 2016. It is the main customs law of its cycle, and Title I carries its name.

Title I sections work on both sides of the border post. Partnership programs for trusted traders are to be improved, and seminars are to train staff to classify and value imports and to police trade with more skill. A joint strategic plan, the Automated Commercial Environment computer system, and the International Trade Data System carry the tech side. Other clauses cover talks on shared recognition deals, the trade advisory panel, Centers of Excellence and Expertise, and risk-based targeting with trade alerts.
plaw-114-126-2016:
Public Law 114-126, the Judicial Redress Act of 2015, extends Privacy Act court rights to citizens of set foreign countries. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. The Privacy Act is the law that guards the personal records federal agencies hold on people, and it lets a person sue over set misuses of those records.

A covered person may sue an agency and gain the same court relief, to the same extent and under the same limits, as a person suing under the Privacy Act. One path covers records shared on purpose or with intent in breach of the act. The other reaches set records, but only against a federal agency or part named under the act. The Attorney General, with the agreement of the Secretaries of State, the Treasury, and Homeland Security, names the covered countries or groups.
plaw-114-127-2016: Public Law 114-127 lets the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma deal in its own land without a federal stamp. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it says the tribe may deal in its own land with no further consent. The tribe may lease, sell, convey, warrant, or hand over any part of its stake in real property that is not held in trust by the United States for the tribe. Trust land is left out in full, and the law that governs trust land transfers is not changed.
plaw-114-128-2016: Public Law 114-128 redraws the lines of set coastal barrier units in Florida by swapping their maps. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it replaces the maps in the official set for the John H Chafee Coastal Barrier Resources System. The old maps for Cape Romano Unit P15, Tigertail Unit FL-63P, and Keewaydin Island Unit P16 give way to new maps dated April 10, 2015, with merged unit labels. The Secretary of the Interior must keep the new maps on file for public viewing.
plaw-114-129-2016:
Public Law 114-129 is a land swap in Danville, Illinois, between the Department of Veterans Affairs and a local college. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. The Secretary of Veterans Affairs may pass land of the Illiana Health Care System in Danville to the Danville Area Community College.

The VA parcel is about 0.6 acres, known as Building Number 48, with any structures on it. In return, the college hands the United States about 1.06 acres with a gazebo, set about 293 feet south of the college library building. The college must take the VA land as it stands. Surveys that satisfy the Secretary fix the exact size and legal lines of both parcels, and the Secretary may add terms to guard the interests of the United States.
plaw-114-130-2016:
Public Law 114-130 hands a veterans care site in Orlando, Florida to the State of Florida. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. The Secretary of Veterans Affairs must pass to the Florida Department of Veterans Affairs all right, title, and claim of the United States in the property known as The Community Living Center. The center is part of the Lake Baldwin Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic, at 5201 Raymond Street in Orlando.

The handover comes with terms. The state must take the property as it stands, and must agree not to apply the VA small house design model for community living centers to it. The deed must state that all the land be used and kept for the sole aim of giving nursing home, live-in, or adult day health care to veterans. Surveys that satisfy the Secretary fix the exact acreage and legal lines.
plaw-114-131-2016: Public Law 114-131 moves one deadline. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it extends the due date for the final report of the Commission on Care. That panel was set up under the Veterans Access, Choice, and Accountability Act of 2014. The old text set the report at no later than 180 days after the panel's first meeting. The act strikes that phrase and inserts a fixed date: not later than June 30, 2016.
plaw-114-132-2016:
Public Law 114-132, the Directing Dollars to Disaster Relief Act of 2015, tells the disaster agency to spend less on its own overhead. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It directs the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency to build a joined plan to cut administrative costs under the Robert T Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act.

The act first defines its terms with care. An administrative cost is a cost the agency bears in support of giving disaster aid for a major disaster, and it leaves out costs borne by a grantee or subgrantee. A direct administrative cost, by contrast, is a cost a grantee bears that can be picked out and tied to one project. The law also defines the hazard mitigation program and the individual assistance program by the Stafford Act sections that allow them.
plaw-114-133-2016:
Public Law 114-133, the Eric Williams Correctional Officer Protection Act of 2015, puts pepper spray in the hands of federal prison staff. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending title 18 of the United States Code. It grants the Director of the Bureau of Prisons power to issue oleoresin capsicum spray, the hot pepper spray used to stop attacks.

A new section 4049 says the Director shall issue the spray as a routine matter. It goes to any officer or worker in a prison that is not minimum or low security who may answer an emergency there. The Director may add more staff as fit. No one may get or carry the spray without first passing a training course on its use, and the course must be retaken each year.
plaw-114-134-2016: Congress named a Grove City post office in Public Law 114-134, passed in 2016. The Ohio site at 2082 Stringtown Road is now the Specialist Joseph W Riley Post Office Building. Federal laws and records use the new name whenever the site comes up. Two sections make up the whole act, one for the naming and one for later references.
plaw-114-135-2016: Public Law 114-135 improves the congressional charter of the Disabled American Veterans, a group chartered in title 36 of the United States Code. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it restates the group's purpose as charitable and educational work. Two aims are added: to teach the public about the sacrifices and needs of disabled veterans, and to teach disabled veterans about the benefits open to them. A new clause sends any assets left at the group's end to the Secretary of Veterans Affairs for the care of disabled veterans.
plaw-114-136-2016:
Public Law 114-136 smooths the handover between presidents. Its name is the Edward Ted Kaufman and Michael Leavitt Presidential Transitions Improvements Act of 2015, and the 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It amends the Presidential Transition Act of 1963 to add a new section on transition work before the election is even held.

The President must take the steps he finds needed to plan and join up executive branch work for a clean transfer of power to the next President. The tools named are a White House transition coordinating council and an agency transition directors council. The text defines the Administrator of General Services, an agency, an eligible candidate, and a Presidential election, and it sets up a Federal Transition Coordinator.
plaw-114-137-2016:
Public Law 114-137, the Competitive Service Act of 2015, lets more hiring officials draw from one list of job candidates. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending section 3318 of title 5 of the United States Code. In federal hiring, an appointing authority asks for a certificate of eligibles, a ranked list of people fit for a post.

For 240 days from the day such a list is issued, a second appointing authority may pick a person from that same list. The post must be in the same job series as the first post and at a like grade level. The first authority may share its list only if the job announcement warned that the list could be used by another authority. The pick must follow the rules the act lays down.
plaw-114-138-2016: For the post office at 99 West 2nd Street in Fond du Lac, Wisconsin, Public Law 114-138 sets a new name: the Lieutenant Colonel James Maggie Megellas Post Office. The act is a 2016 law of the 114th Congress. The name holds in all federal maps, rules, and papers that touch the site.
plaw-114-139-2016:
Public Law 114-139 orders a plan to win Taiwan a seat, as an observer, in the world police body INTERPOL. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It directs the Secretary of State to build a strategy to gain observer status for Taiwan in the International Criminal Police Organization.

The findings make the case. Shared word on crime helps all police forces keep people safe, the act says, and open access to INTERPOL aids every nation. Taiwan held full membership from 1964 through its National Police Administration, but was cast out in 1984 when the People's Republic of China applied to join. Without a seat, Taiwan cannot reach INTERPOL's I-24/7 global police communications system, which gives live word on criminals and crime across borders.
plaw-114-140-2016:
Public Law 114-140, the Evidence-Based Policymaking Commission Act of 2016, sets up a panel to study how the government can use its own data to judge what works. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It creates the Commission on Evidence-Based Policymaking inside the executive branch.

The commission has 15 members. Three are named by the President. They are a researcher, data expert, or program manager; an expert in guarding personal data and keeping data use small; and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. The third seat may be filled by that Director's stand-in. The Speaker of the House and the House Minority Leader name three each, on the same pattern, and the Senate Majority Leader names three as well.
plaw-114-141-2016:
Public Law 114-141, the Airport and Airway Extension Act of 2016, keeps the nation's airport programs running for a set span. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It amends title 49 of the United States Code and the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.

Title I extends the airport improvement program and a row of powers that were set to lapse. Its sections cover Federal Aviation Administration operations, air navigation facilities and gear, and research and development. One clause checks the work against the aviation funding rule, and one covers the essential air service program for small towns. Title II holds the money side: spending power from the Airport and Airway Trust Fund, and an extension of the taxes that feed that fund.
plaw-114-142-2016: Public Law 114-142, the Foreclosure Relief and Extension for Servicemembers Act of 2015, moves two dates by two years. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it amends the same 2012 veterans law that an act of 2014 had already stretched once. The longer shield that guards service members from mortgage foreclosure and eviction now ends on December 31, 2017 in place of December 31, 2015. A linked start date moves from January 1, 2016 to January 1, 2018.
plaw-114-143-2016:
Public Law 114-143, the Integrated Public Alert and Warning System Modernization Act of 2015, orders an upgrade of the nation's emergency alert system. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending the Homeland Security Act of 2002. It directs the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency to modernize the integrated public alert and warning system.

A new section 526 states the goal: timely and sound warnings about natural disasters, acts of terrorism, and other man-made disasters or threats to public safety. Under all conditions, the President, federal agencies, and state, tribal, and local governments must be able to alert and warn people in areas at risk, with the President's use coming first. The Administrator must set shared protocols, standards, terms, and steps for the work.
plaw-114-144-2016:
Public Law 114-144, the Older Americans Act Reauthorization Act of 2016, renews the Older Americans Act of 1965, the main law on services for older people. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. Much of the act is careful redefinition of the terms the older law runs on.

Abuse is defined as the knowing infliction of physical or mental harm, or the knowing withholding of goods or services needed to meet basic needs or to avoid such harm. Adult protective services take in taking reports of abuse, neglect, or exploitation, probing them, and case work, plus arranging medical, social, legal, housing, and police help. An Aging and Disability Resource Center is a state body that gives older people and people with disabilities one joined path into long-term care.
plaw-114-145-2016:
Public Law 114-145, the Ensuring Patient Access and Effective Drug Enforcement Act of 2016, balances two goals in its name: patient access to prescription drugs and firm action against drug diversion. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It works on the registration process under the Controlled Substances Act, the system that licenses firms to make and sell set drugs.

The act pins down two phrases. Factors tied to public health and safety mean factors that fit the findings in section 101 of that law. Imminent danger means a strong chance of an immediate threat of death, grave bodily harm, or abuse of a drug, because a registrant failed to keep sound controls against diversion. A later clause gives registrants a chance to file a corrective action plan before a license is suspended or taken away.
plaw-114-146-2016: Public Law 114-146, the Adding Zika Virus to the FDA Priority Review Voucher Program Act, does what its name says. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it amends section 524(a)(3) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the list of tropical diseases in the priority review voucher program. That program rewards firms that win approval for a drug for a listed disease with a voucher for faster review of a later drug. Zika Virus Disease joins the list as item R, and Filoviruses becomes Filovirus Diseases.
plaw-114-147-2016:
Public Law 114-147, the National POW/MIA Remembrance Act of 2015, places an empty chair in the United States Capitol. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. The chair honors American Prisoners of War and those Missing in Action, and it bears the logo of the National League of POW/MIA Families.

Congress finds that such chairs have been placed in prominent spots across the United States in recent years, and that the Capitol is a fit place for one. The Architect of the Capitol must strike a deal to obtain the chair and place it in a fit permanent spot within two years of the act. The Architect may work with tax-exempt charities to seek private gifts, and may take gifts of funds, property, and services to pay for the work.
plaw-114-148-2016:
Public Law 114-148, the Breast Cancer Awareness Commemorative Coin Act, orders a coin to mark the fight against breast cancer. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It tells the Secretary of the Treasury to mint coins in recognition of that fight.

The findings give the scale of the disease. Breast cancer is the most common cancer among American women apart from skin cancers. About one in eight women will develop the invasive form in her lifetime, up from one in eleven in 1975. It is the second leading cause of cancer death in women, with a risk of death of about one in 36, though death rates have fallen since about 1989. The findings count 16.5 billion dollars spent a year on treatment in the United States, and name finding a cure as a goal of the government.
plaw-114-149-2016: Public Law 114-149 renames a military site in Montana. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it renames the Armed Forces Reserve Center in Great Falls as the Captain John E Moran and Captain William Wylie Galt Armed Forces Reserve Center. From then on, any mention of that center in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of the new name. The enrolled text repeats the word map in its references clause, a slip that ships with the law as passed.
plaw-114-150-2016:
Public Law 114-150, the Department of Homeland Security Headquarters Consolidation Accountability Act of 2015, demands a full account of a big building project. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to send Congress word on the department's headquarters consolidation project in the National Capital Region.

The report is due within 120 days and is built with the Administrator named in the text. It is tied to the improved plan cleared by the Office of Management and Budget for the fiscal year 2016 budget. It must give a plan for who will sit at the site: which department-wide, component, and support offices, how many full-time staff, and the seat-to-staff ratio, with dates for the move. It must also weigh the gap between the space the department has now and what it will need, and give a current build plan for the St Elizabeths campus.
plaw-114-151-2016:
Public Law 114-151, the Protect and Preserve International Cultural Property Act, guards art and old sites put at risk by war and unrest. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. Its heading speaks of cultural property at risk from political instability, armed conflict, and natural or other disasters.

The sense of Congress urges the President to set up a cross-agency panel, led by a State Department official of Assistant Secretary rank or higher. The panel should take in the Smithsonian Institution and the agencies charged with such work. It should talk with groups such as the United States Committee of the Blue Shield, museums, schools, and the art market. Its aims join guarding property and sites, stopping looting and illegal trade that funds terrorist and criminal groups, and allowing lawful exchange. A later section gives emergency protection for Syrian property.
plaw-114-152-2016:
Public Law 114-152, the National Bison Legacy Act, adopts the bison as the national mammal of the United States. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. The findings that open the act treat the bison as a historic symbol of the country. They bind it up with the economic and spiritual lives of many Indian tribes, through trade and sacred rites.

More than 60 tribes take part in the Intertribal Buffalo Council, the findings say, and tribal herds graze on more than 1,000,000 acres of tribal land. A small band of ranchers saved the bison from dying out in the late 1800s by gathering the last of the herds. The American Bison Society was formed in 1905 by William Hornaday, Theodore Roosevelt, and others. As of 2012, private producers kept 162,110 head of bison, a source of jobs and of healthy meat.
plaw-114-153-2016:
Public Law 114-153, the Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016, gives trade secret theft a federal court path. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending chapter 90 of title 18 of the United States Code. Trade secrets are know-how a firm keeps hidden, the source of its edge, and theft of them was once mainly a state court matter.

The owner of a secret that has been misused may sue in federal court. The suit lies if the secret is tied to a product or service used, or meant for use, in interstate or foreign commerce. In rare cases, on a sworn claim, a court may order the seizure of property needed to stop the secret from spreading. The court must find clear facts that a normal court order would fall short, since the other party would dodge or evade it.
plaw-114-154-2016:
Public Law 114-154, the Transnational Drug Trafficking Act of 2015, gives the Department of Justice more tools against drug trafficking that crosses borders. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It works through section 1009 of the Controlled Substances Import and Export Act.

The act makes it unlawful to make or distribute a schedule I or II drug, flunitrazepam, or a listed chemical with the wrong intent. The intent is meaning, knowing, or having good cause to think the goods will be smuggled into the United States, or into waters within 12 miles of its coast. A like ban covers making or spreading a listed chemical meant for use in making a drug that will be smuggled in. A second section turns to trafficking in counterfeit goods or services, amending chapter 113 of title 18.
plaw-114-155-2016:
Public Law 114-155, the Bulletproof Vest Partnership Grant Program Reauthorization Act of 2015, renews a grant program that helps police buy body armor. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968.

The funding line is set at 25,000,000 dollars for each of the fiscal years 2016 through 2020. Money from those years that is not pledged by December 31, 2022 must move to the General Fund of the Treasury by January 31, 2023. A sense of Congress clause says the funds should stay open through the end of the first fiscal year after the year they were granted, not until spent. A matching funds limit follows in the text.
plaw-114-156-2016:
Public Law 114-156, the Fallen Heroes Flag Act of 2016, gives a Capitol-flown flag to the families of public safety workers killed on duty. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. A Capitol-flown flag is a flag of the United States flown over the Capitol in honor of the person who died.

At the request of an immediate family member, the family's Representative or Senator may give the family such a flag. The fallen may be a firefighter, a law enforcement officer, a member of a rescue squad or ambulance crew, or a public safety officer. Immediate family takes in a spouse, parent, brother, sister, or child, a person who stood in a parent's place, and any other kin by blood or marriage.
plaw-114-157-2016: Public Law 114-157 updates dated words for minorities in two older laws. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it amends the Department of Energy Organization Act and the Local Public Works Capital Development and Investment Act of 1976. Old lists that named groups with terms such as Negro, Oriental, and Eskimo are struck. In their place both clauses now read Asian American, Native Hawaiian, Pacific Islander, African American, Hispanic, Puerto Rican, Native American, or Alaska Native. Small shifts in word form fit each clause.
plaw-114-158-2016:
Public Law 114-158 opens Arlington National Cemetery, in a narrow way, to the ashes of a set class of veterans. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending title 38 of the United States Code. The act covers people whose service has been ruled to be active service, a finding made under a clause of the GI Bill Improvement Act of 1977.

The Secretary of the Army must make sure the cremated remains of such a person can be placed above ground in the cemetery, with military honors under section 1491 of title 10. The rule reaches remains not yet laid to rest when the act passed, and people who die on or after that day. A second section orders a report within 180 days on the burial and inurnment capacity of the cemetery, to the veterans and armed services panels of both houses.
plaw-114-159-2016:
Public Law 114-159, the American Manufacturing Competitiveness Act of 2016, sets up a clean process for asking Congress to pause or cut import duties. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. The process feeds the miscellaneous tariff bill, the law that drops duties on goods United States makers cannot get at home.

The findings say the tariff schedule now taxes many imported goods with no home supply, or too little of it, and that such taxes warp the economy and hurt makers and buyers. A regular, open path for petitions builds trust that the process is fair and free of abuse. The act also states that a bill built this way will hold no congressional earmarks or limited tax benefits, as the rules of the House and Senate define them.
plaw-114-160-2016: Washington, District of Columbia gains a renamed federal building under Public Law 114-160 of 2016. Its site at 99 New York Avenue NE takes the name Ariel Rios Federal Building. That name is the one federal records must use for the building. The whole law is that naming, plus a rule that later references follow the new name.
plaw-114-161-2016:
Public Law 114-161 moves a federal parcel in Alaska to the city that hosts it. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It directs the Administrator of General Services, acting for the Archivist of the United States, to pass set federal land in Alaska to the Municipality of Anchorage.

The parcel is about nine acres with structures, at 400 East Fortieth Avenue, run by the National Archives and Records Administration. Once a survey and appraisal are done, the land is offered to the city by quitclaim deed, on the terms the act names. The city pays the cost of the appraisal and any other costs of the handover. A survey the city pays for, and that satisfies the Archivist, fixes the exact size and legal lines of the land.
plaw-114-162-2016:
Public Law 114-162 renews the National Estuary Program and adds a contest for its funds. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, the main clean water law. Estuaries are the bays and inlets where rivers meet the sea, and the program guards their health.

A new clause in section 320(g) tells the Administrator to make competitive awards from set funds. State, interstate, and regional water agencies, coastal zone bodies, other public or nonprofit groups, and even single applicants may apply. Winners are to be those best able to meet urgent threats to the health and wealth of coastal areas. The threats named are wide seagrass losses, repeated harmful algae blooms, and strange marine mammal deaths. Invading species, jellyfish swarms in tourist season, flooding tied to sea level rise, and low oxygen in estuary waters are named as well.
plaw-114-163-2016:
Public Law 114-163 keeps a toll bridge over the Rio Grande in private hands with no end date. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It amends Public Law 87-532, the law that let the Starr-Camargo Bridge Company build and run a bridge near Rio Grande City, Texas.

The changes add the company's successors and assigns to the grant, so the right to run the bridge can pass on. The bridge and its approaches may run to no more than 14 lanes. A clause that ended the grant 66 years after the bridge was finished is struck. A new section gives the company and its heirs the same rights the B and P Bridge Company holds under a 1928 act. Those rights must be used under the fair pay and public hearing rules of Texas law.
plaw-114-164-2016: Public Law 114-164 names a veterans clinic in Tennessee, and its findings tell why. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it names the Department of Veterans Affairs community-based outpatient clinic at 1124 Blanton Drive in Sevierville the Dannie A Carr Veterans Outpatient Clinic. Specialist Four Dannie A Carr of Sevier County served in the Vietnam War, was twice wounded, and was killed by artillery fire on July 3, 1969. He held the Bronze Star for Valor and the Purple Heart, and the towns of his county backed the naming.
plaw-114-165-2016:
Public Law 114-165, the Native American Children's Safety Act, demands criminal record checks before a tribal court places a child in foster care. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It amends the Indian Child Protection and Family Violence Prevention Act.

A new clause in section 408 gives the job to the tribal social services agency. A covered individual is any person 18 or older, plus anyone the agency picks for a check. A foster care placement is a move that takes an Indian child from a parent or Indian custodian into a foster home, an institution, or a guardian's home. In such a move, the parent cannot take the child back on demand. The clause covers cases where parental rights still stand, and cases where they have ended but the child has not been placed for good.
plaw-114-166-2016: Renaming one post office is the whole of Public Law 114-166, passed by the 114th Congress in 2016. The Camp Pendleton site in the 1103 USPS Building becomes the Camp Pendleton Medal of Honor Post Office. All federal references to the site are read as references to the new name. A second section settles how the site is cited in federal papers after the change.
plaw-114-167-2016: Public Law 114-167 names a post office in Pennsylvania for a soldier who gave his life for his crew. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it names the Postal Service site at 523 East Railroad Street in Knox the Specialist Ross A McGinnis Memorial Post Office. The findings quote his Medal of Honor citation. In Baghdad on December 4, 2006, a grenade fell through the gunner's hatch of his vehicle. He warned his four crew members before the blast that killed him.
plaw-114-168-2016: In California, the post office at 1048 West Robinhood Drive in Stockton takes a new name under Public Law 114-168. It becomes the W Ronald Coale Memorial Post Office Building. The 114th Congress passed the naming act in 2016. Federal laws, maps, rules, and records must use that name for the site from then on.

plaw-114-177-2016: One post office in Cedar Rapids, Iowa is renamed by Public Law 114-177, an act of the 114th Congress from 2016. plaw-114-178-2016:
Public Law 114-178, the Indian Trust Asset Reform Act, reforms how tribal trust assets are run. Trust assets are the lands and funds the United States holds for Indian tribes. The 114th Congress passed the act in 2016.

Title I states findings and restates the trust duty the government owes. Title II sets up an Indian trust asset management demonstration project. Tribes are picked to take part, draw up their own management plans, and run forest land work and surface leasing under them. Title III aims at speed and leaner process. It covers an Under Secretary for Indian Affairs, the Office of Special Trustee for American Indians, appraisals and valuations, and cost savings.
plaw-114-179-2016: In Oregon, the Department of Veterans Affairs clinic at 704 Veterans Drive in The Dalles takes a new name under Public Law 114-179. It becomes the Loren R Kaufman VA Clinic. The 114th Congress passed the naming act in 2016. Federal laws, maps, rules, and records must use that name for the site from then on.
plaw-114-180-2016:
Public Law 114-180, the Federal Law Enforcement Self-Defense and Protection Act of 2015, keeps federal officers armed for their own defense during a furlough. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. A covered furlough is a shutdown span when officers are sent home without pay, and the act's concern is that they stay targets in that span.

The findings put numbers on the risk. In 2012 alone, 1,857 federal law enforcement officers were assaulted, 206 of them gravely hurt, and 8,587 more were assaulted from 2008 through 2011. Officers stay targets off duty too: 27 were killed off duty in the past three years. The act then defines its terms, starting with agency and with a covered officer, a worker of an agency who may make arrests or prosecute federal crimes.
plaw-114-181-2016: Public Law 114-181 takes federal land in California into trust for a tribe. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it takes about 301 acres in Lassen County into trust for the Susanville Indian Rancheria. The land is run by the Bureau of Land Management and shown on a December 31, 2014 map. Valid rights others already hold are kept. One bar is stated in plain terms: class II and class III gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act may never run on the land.
plaw-114-182-2016:
Public Law 114-182, the Frank R Lautenberg Chemical Safety for the 21st Century Act, modernizes the Toxic Substances Control Act, the main law on industrial chemicals. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. Title I is named Chemical Safety.

The contents show a full rebuild. Sections cover testing of chemicals and mixtures, notices before making or processing them, and a system to rank chemicals, weigh their risks, and regulate them. Imminent hazards, reporting and record keeping, and the place of secret business information all get sections. The act ties the work to other federal laws and to state programs, sets penalties, and allows suits by citizens. Exports of elemental mercury get their own clause, and one section is named Trevor's Law.
plaw-114-183-2016:
Public Law 114-183 pairs a plain name with an acronym: the Protecting our Infrastructure of Pipelines and Enhancing Safety Act of 2016, or the PIPES Act of 2016. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending title 49 of the United States Code to raise safety in pipeline transport.

The contents run from funding and rule updates to reviews of integrity management for natural gas and for hazardous liquids, the checks that catch weak pipe before it fails. Technical safety standards panels, inspection report information, and better damage prevention tools follow. Later sections cover workforce management, an information-sharing system, a nationwide pipeline safety database, underground gas storage sites, joint inspections, emergency order power, and response plans.
plaw-114-184-2016:
Public Law 114-184, the Recovering Missing Children Act, lets tax data be shared to help find lost children. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending section 6103 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. That section keeps tax returns secret, with narrow gates for sharing.

The act adds the case of a missing or exploited child to the gates in the law enforcement clause. A federal agency head, or a stand-in, may pass return data gained under that clause to state and local officers. That may be done only for a probe into such a case, and only where the state or local agency is part of a team. The edits also let criminal probes and court cases tied to a missing or exploited child use the shared data.
plaw-114-185-2016:
Public Law 114-185, the FOIA Improvement Act of 2016, strengthens the Freedom of Information Act, the law that lets any person ask federal agencies for their records. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending section 552 of title 5 of the United States Code.

Agencies must now offer set records for public viewing in an electronic format, not just for copying in a reading room. The list grows to take in copies of all records already released to any person. It covers records asked for three or more times, or that the agency finds are likely to be asked for again. A fee clause bars an agency from charging search fees when it has missed a time limit set by the law.
plaw-114-186-2016:
Public Law 114-186, the Fraud Reduction and Data Analytics Act of 2015, tells federal agencies to hunt fraud with better controls and better use of data. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. Its heading speaks of financial and management controls to weigh and cut fraud risks, and of data analytics to spot, stop, and answer fraud, improper payments among it.

Within 90 days, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, in talks with the Comptroller General, must set guidelines for agencies. Each agency is to build controls that spot and weigh fraud risks and that prevent, detect, and answer fraud. The guidelines must take in the lead practices from a July 28, 2015 Government Accountability Office report, a framework for managing fraud risks in federal programs.
plaw-114-187-2016:
Public Law 114-187 is PROMESA, the Puerto Rico Oversight, Management, and Economic Stability Act. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, as Puerto Rico faced a debt crisis. One oddity sits at the head of the text. Its opening line speaks of the National Sea Grant College Program Act, while the title, the short name, and every title that follows are PROMESA's own.

Title I sets up a Financial Oversight and Management Board, with its place, staff, powers, budget, and ethics rules, and shields it from blame for claims. Title II lists the board's duties: clearing fiscal plans and budgets, ruling on what happens when a budget breaks the plan, checking that work fits the plan, and advising on sound finances. It also covers the board's part in restructuring the island's debts.
plaw-114-188-2016: Public Law 114-188, the Female Veteran Suicide Prevention Act, tells the Department of Veterans Affairs to judge its care through the eyes of women veterans. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it amends section 1709B of title 38 of the United States Code. When the Secretary weighs mental health care and suicide prevention programs, the measures used must take in metrics that apply to women in particular. The review must name the programs that work best for women veterans and those with the highest satisfaction rates among them.
plaw-114-189-2016:
Public Law 114-189 funds jobs for veterans in an unlikely craft: caring for old artifacts. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It gives the Army Corps of Engineers money to hire veterans and service members to help with curation and historic preservation work.

The findings explain the need. Federal agencies must preserve and catalogue artifacts dug up in their work, and uncatalogued pieces sit in hundreds of stores and museums across the country. The Corps began the Veterans' Curation Program in October 2009, hiring Iraq and Afghanistan veterans to sort, clean, and catalogue its collections. Workers gain skills in databases, records, photography, and writing. Of 203 graduates, 87 percent found lasting work in a tied field or went back to school.
plaw-114-190-2016:
Public Law 114-190, the FAA Extension, Safety, and Security Act of 2016, keeps aviation programs funded and adds safety and security rules. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It amends title 49 of the United States Code and the tax code, stretching the funding and spending power of the Airport and Airway Trust Fund.

Title I is the extension itself. The airport improvement program, lapsing powers, Federal Aviation Administration operations, air navigation gear, and research all run on, with the essential air service program for small towns among them. Title II is named Aviation Safety Critical Reforms. Its safety subtitle opens with a deadline for the pilot records database and a section on cockpit automation management.
plaw-114-191-2016:
Public Law 114-191, the Foreign Aid Transparency and Accountability Act of 2016, tells the President to set guidelines for United States foreign aid programs. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. The aim, in its heading, is open books and clear proof of what aid does.

The act defines evaluation with care. It is the steady gathering and study of facts about a program's traits and results. The facts are used to judge the program, to make it work better, and to guide choices on current and future work. Covered aid is aid allowed under part I of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, with set carve-outs. The panels named as the right ones to deal with are the foreign affairs and appropriations panels of both houses.
plaw-114-192-2016: Public Law 114-192 gives a new name to the post office at 15 Rochester Street in Bergen, New York: the Barry G Miller Post Office. Congress passed the act in 2016. From then on, federal records refer to the site by that name. Two sections make up the whole act, one for the naming and one for later references.
plaw-114-193-2016: The Postal Service site at 525 N Broadway in Aurora, Illinois becomes the Kenneth M Christy Post Office Building under Public Law 114-193. The 114th Congress passed the naming act in 2016. Any federal mention of the site counts as a mention of the new name. Nothing else changes: the act pairs the naming with a short rule on references.
plaw-114-194-2016: Public Law 114-194, the Venezuela Defense of Human Rights and Civil Society Extension Act of 2016, keeps a sanctions law alive for three more years. Passed by the 114th Congress, it amends section 5(e) of the Venezuela Defense of Human Rights and Civil Society Act of 2014. That act placed targeted sanctions tied to abuse of protesters. The end date in that clause moves from December 31, 2016 to December 31, 2019. The act makes no other change.
plaw-114-195-2016:
Public Law 114-195, the Global Food Security Act of 2016, sets a joined strategy for United States aid against hunger abroad. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. Its heading speaks of cutting world poverty and hunger, of farm-led growth that takes in all, of better nutrition for women and children, and of strength for people at risk.

The findings open with a count from the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations: 805,000,000 people in the world live with chronic hunger. Hunger and poor nutrition rob people of health and full lives and stunt the growth of the next generation, the act says. It quotes a 2014 threat assessment with a warning. Lack of food can shake countries that matter to United States security. It can also hand armed groups a chance to use aid and blame governments.
plaw-114-196-2016:
Public Law 114-196, the United States Semiquincentennial Commission Act of 2016, sets up the panel that will plan the nation's 250th birthday. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. Semiquincentennial is the word for a 250th anniversary, and the date in view is July 4, 2026.

Congress finds that the anniversary of the founding of the United States holds major weight in the nation's heritage. The founding is marked by the Declaration of Independence in 1776. Its heritage is one of liberty, representative government, and equal rights that cannot be taken away. The commission is to plan, spur, build, and join up the marking of the day through local, state, national, and world events. Its members are to speak for the right public and private bodies and groups.
plaw-114-197-2016:
Public Law 114-197, the Veterans' Compensation COLA Act of 2016, raises monthly checks for veterans hurt in service and for their survivors. COLA stands for cost-of-living adjustment. The 114th Congress passed the act in 2016, and the rise takes effect on December 1, 2016.

The Secretary of Veterans Affairs must raise the dollar sums in force on November 30, 2016. The sums span wartime disability compensation, added pay for dependents, and the clothing allowance. They also span dependency and indemnity compensation for a surviving spouse and for children. Each sum rises by the same rate as Social Security benefits for that date, as set under section 215(i) of the Social Security Act.
plaw-114-198-2016:
Public Law 114-198, the Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act of 2016, is the big federal answer to the opioid crisis. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It grants the Attorney General and the Secretary of Health and Human Services power to award grants against prescription opioid abuse and heroin use.

Title I covers prevention and education. It sets up a task force on pain management, awareness campaigns, and grants that strengthen town coalitions against local drug crises. It orders an FDA opioid action plan, research at the National Institutes of Health, and better access to overdose treatment and to reversal drugs, with grants for both. Title II joins law enforcement and treatment, opening with a broad opioid abuse grant program, first responder training, and wider drug take-back programs.
plaw-114-199-2016: Public Law 114-199, the Protecting Our Lives by Initiating COPS Expansion Act of 2016, is known as the POLICE Act for short. Passed by the 114th Congress, it amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968. One use joins the list of things COPS grant money may pay for: taking part in nationally known active shooter training programs. The courses named are scenario-based, joined response classes built to counter active shooter threats and acts of terrorism against people or facilities.
plaw-114-200-2016: Congress named a Jackson Heights post office in Public Law 114-200, passed in 2016. The New York site at 7802 37th Avenue is now the Jeanne and Jules Manford Post Office Building. Federal laws and records use the new name whenever the site comes up. The whole law is that naming, plus a rule that later references follow the new name.
plaw-114-201-2016:
Public Law 114-201, the Housing Opportunity Through Modernization Act of 2016, updates the main federal housing programs. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. Its heading speaks of giving housing chances in the United States through the modernization of housing programs of many kinds.

Title I covers Section 8 rental aid and public housing. Its sections set rules for inspecting homes, reviewing tenant income, and capping how long a family whose income has grown too high may stay in public housing. Asset limits for aid, fair market rent setting, and the gathering of utility data all appear. The list runs to vouchers for manufactured housing and a family unification program for children aging out of foster care. Title II turns to rural housing.
plaw-114-202-2016: For the post office at 620 Central Avenue in Hot Springs National Park, Arkansas, Public Law 114-202 sets a new name: the Chief Petty Officer Adam Brown United States Post Office. The act is a 2016 law of the 114th Congress. The name holds in all federal maps, rules, and papers that touch the site.
plaw-114-203-2016: Elfers, Florida gains a renamed post office under Public Law 114-203 of 2016. Its site at 4122 Madison Street takes the name Private First Class Felton Roger Fussell Memorial Post Office. That name is the one federal records must use for the site. A second section settles how the site is cited in federal papers after the change.
plaw-114-204-2016: Renaming one post office is the whole of Public Law 114-204, passed by the 114th Congress in 2016. The Phoenix site at 522 North Central Avenue becomes the Ed Pastor Post Office. plaw-114-206-2016: One post office in Riverdale, Georgia is renamed by Public Law 114-206, an act of the 114th Congress from 2016. plaw-114-207-2016: Public Law 114-207 gives a new name to the post office at 61 South Baldwin Avenue in Sierra Madre, California: the Louis Van Iersel Post Office. Congress passed the act in 2016. From then on, federal records refer to the site by that name. Two sections make up the whole act, one for the naming and one for later references.
plaw-114-208-2016: The Postal Service site at 1301 Alabama Avenue in Selma, Alabama becomes the Amelia Boynton Robinson Post Office Building under Public Law 114-208. The 114th Congress passed the naming act in 2016. Any federal mention of the site counts as a mention of the new name. Nothing else changes: the act pairs the naming with a short rule on references.
plaw-114-209-2016: Congress named a Sugar Land post office in Public Law 114-209, passed in 2016. The Texas site at 3130 Grants Lake Boulevard is now the LCpl Garrett W Gamble, USMC Post Office Building. Federal laws and records use the new name whenever the site comes up. The whole law is that naming, plus a rule that later references follow the new name.
plaw-114-210-2016:
Public Law 114-210 spells out its own acronym: the Making Electronic Government Accountable By Yielding Tangible Efficiencies Act of 2016, or the MEGABYTE Act. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. It tells the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to issue a directive on the management of software licenses across the government.

Each agency's Chief Information Officer must build a full software licensing policy. It must set clear roles, duties, and one central watch post for enterprise and commercial licenses. The officer must build a full inventory, taking in 80 percent of license spending, with machine tools that find and count licenses. Licenses must be tracked through their life cycle, usage data studied to make cost-effective choices, and staff trained for the work.
plaw-114-211-2016: For the post office at 229 West Main Cross Street in Findlay, Ohio, Public Law 114-211 sets a new name: the Michael Garver Oxley Memorial Post Office Building. The act is a 2016 law of the 114th Congress. The name holds in all federal maps, rules, and papers that touch the site. A second section settles how the site is cited in federal papers after the change.
plaw-114-212-2016: Omaha, Nebraska gains a renamed post office under Public Law 114-212 of 2016. Its site at 5720 South 142nd Street takes the name Petty Officer 1st Class Caleb A Nelson Post Office Building. That name is the one federal records must use for the site. The law does nothing more than rename the site and align later references with the new name.
plaw-114-213-2016: Renaming one post office is the whole of Public Law 114-213, passed by the 114th Congress in 2016. The Laurel Hill site at 3957 2nd Avenue becomes the Sergeant First Class William Kelly Lacey Post Office. All federal references to the site are read as references to the new name. The act has two parts: the naming itself, and a rule for how later references to the site are read.
plaw-114-214-2016: In Michigan, the post office at 10721 E Jefferson Ave in Detroit takes a new name under Public Law 114-214. It becomes the Mary E McCoy Post Office Building. The 114th Congress passed the naming act in 2016. Federal laws, maps, rules, and records must use that name for the site from then on.
plaw-114-215-2016:
Public Law 114-215, the John F Kennedy Centennial Commission Act, sets up a panel to mark the 100th anniversary of the birth of John F Kennedy. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016. A centennial is a hundredth anniversary, and Kennedy was born in 1917.

The commission must plan, build, and carry out the acts it finds fitting and proper to honor Kennedy on that day. It must advise and aid federal, state, and local agencies and civic groups that hold their own events. It must also shape acts the federal government itself may carry out, and report to the President and Congress. The panel has 11 members, among them the Secretary of the Interior and four named by the President. Those four are picked with the advice of the Board of Trustees of the John F Kennedy Library Foundation.
plaw-114-216-2016:
Public Law 114-216 carries a catalog title about the National Sea Grant College Program, but the law it enacts is about food labels. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, and its first section is headed National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard. That standard is added to the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 as a new subtitle.

Bioengineering, for a food, means food that holds genetic material changed by in vitro recombinant DNA work, where the change could not come from standard breeding or be found in nature. The standard binds any claim in a disclosure that a food is a bioengineered food. It reaches only food under the labeling rules of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act that is meant for human use. The Secretary in the text is the Secretary of Agriculture.
plaw-114-217-2016:
Public Law 114-217 renews the Library of Congress programs that save the nation's sound and film heritage. Its full name is the Library of Congress Sound Recording and Film Preservation Programs Reauthorization Act of 2016, and the 114th Congress passed it in 2016.

On the sound side, the National Recording Preservation Board runs through fiscal year 2026 in place of 2016. The National Recording Preservation Foundation is funded through 2026 as well. Its cap is the lesser of 1,000,000 dollars or a sum the text ties to gifts. Its board grows from nine directors to twelve. On the film side, the National Film Preservation Board and the National Film Preservation Foundation both gain the same ten-year reach, through 2026.
plaw-114-218-2016:
Public Law 114-218, the Department of Veterans Affairs Dental Insurance Reauthorization Act of 2016, gives veterans a dental insurance plan through the VA. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016, amending title 38 of the United States Code. Dental care is a gap for many veterans who do not qualify for VA dental treatment itself.

A new section 1712C tells the Secretary to set up and run the plan. It covers any veteran enrolled in the VA patient system, and any survivor or dependent of a veteran who can gain VA medical care under section 1781. The Secretary must contract with a dental insurer to run the plan. The text then lays out the benefits the plan must give.
plaw-114-219-2016: Public Law 114-219 widens the gear a library service may lend to blind readers. Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, it lets the National Library Service for the Blind and Physically Handicapped provide playback equipment in all formats. The act amends the 1931 law to provide books for the adult blind: words tying the buying, upkeep, and replacement of reproducers to sound-reproduction recordings are struck. In their place, the reproducers may serve any such forms the service provides.
plaw-114-220-2016: Public Law 114-220, passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, gives a new name to a health clinic for veterans. The clinic is the Department of Veterans Affairs site in Laughlin, Nevada. After the act took effect, the clinic is known as the Master Chief Petty Officer Jesse Dean VA Clinic. Any mention of the old clinic in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the clinic under its new name.
plaw-114-221-2016:
Congress passed Public Law 114-221 in 2016 as the Native American Tourism and Improving Visitor Experience Act, also called the NATIVE Act. The law, from the 114th Congress, aims to grow tourism tied to Native American heritage and culture.

The act lists clear goals. It seeks to join Native tourism with the national travel plan, help tribes and Native Hawaiian groups take part more fully, and draw more guests to rural and remote places. It also backs grants, loans, and skilled help to build roads and sites, raise tourism work, and lift living standards in Native towns.
plaw-114-222-2016:
Justice Against Sponsors of Terrorism Act is the short title of Public Law 114-222, passed by the 114th Congress in 2016. The act aims to deter acts of terror and to give justice to victims. Congress states those goals at the start of the text.

Early findings say world terror is a grave threat to the United States. They note that some terror groups raise large funds abroad for acts aimed at the United States. The findings also say the law must treat help for terror, and plots to aid it, as grounds for a civil case in court.
plaw-114-223-2016:
Public Law 114-223, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, keeps the federal government funded for fiscal year 2017. Its long title joins three parts: a funds act for defense building and veterans, a Zika response act, and a stopgap funds act.

The contents list four divisions. Division A funds defense building, the veterans agency, and linked agencies, plus war costs and general rules. Division B funds the Zika response through the health and state agencies. Division C gives stopgap funds for 2017, and Division D cancels some funds. The act also sets rules on how long the funds stay open for use.
plaw-114-224-2016:
Passed in 2016, Public Law 114-224 creates a group to mark a key date for the Virgin Islands of the United States. The 114th Congress set up the Virgin Islands of the United States Centennial Commission by this act. The date marks 100 years since the islands became a territory of the United States.

The group must plan and run events for the 100th year. It must also advise federal, state, and local agencies and civic groups that hold linked events. The act sets the group at eight members, drawn from the Interior agency, the islands' governor, the House, and the Senate, and calls for reports to the President and Congress.
plaw-114-225-2016: Public Law 114-225, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, names a border post in Texas. The post is the Customs and Border Protection Port of Entry at 1400 Lower Island Road in Tornillo, Texas. Under the act, the post is known as the Marcelino Serna Port of Entry. Any mention of that post in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the post under its new name.
plaw-114-226-2016:
West Los Angeles Leasing Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-226, passed by the 114th Congress. The act lets the Secretary of Veterans Affairs sign some leases at the agency's West Los Angeles Campus in Los Angeles, California. It also makes some fixes to the agency's lease powers.

The leases named in the sample serve veterans and their families. One kind gives homes with support for veterans on agency land. A second kind, for terms up to 50 years, lets a third party give help such as health and wellness work, schooling, job training, and peer events. It also covers aid with legal issues and federal benefits.
plaw-114-227-2016: Public Law 114-227, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, concerns a war memorial in France. The act changes title 36 of the United States Code. It lets the American Battle Monuments Commission make a deal with the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial Foundation. Under that deal, the Commission may acquire, run, and keep up the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial in Marnes-la-Coquette, France. The site holds a cemetery with the remains of 49 United States fliers who died in World War I, and the Commission must keep the site in good care.
plaw-114-228-2016:
Congress titled Public Law 114-228 the Department of Veterans Affairs Expiring Authorities Act of 2016. Passed by the 114th Congress, the act extends some parts of title 38 law that were set to end. Those parts are run by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.

The contents list shows the health care title first. It extends fees for hospital and nursing home care, nursing home care for some veterans with wounds from service, and funds for help to caregivers. It also extends cost claims from third parties, a child care pilot, grants to move rural veterans, and a retreat program for women veterans.
plaw-114-229-2016:
Advancing Hope Act of 2016 is the short title of Public Law 114-229, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress wrote the act for one main job: to extend a fast-review voucher program. That program rewards work on drugs for rare diseases in children.

The act makes precise changes to the food and drug law. It states that a rare disease in this program is a grave or life-threatening disease whose worst effects hit people from birth to age 18. It also sets a notice rule: a firm that wants a voucher must tell the Secretary of its plan when it files its drug request, starting 90 days after the act.
plaw-114-230-2016:
Korean War Veterans Memorial Wall of Remembrance Act is Public Law 114-230, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The act lets a new wall be built as part of the Korean War Veterans Memorial. Private gifts may pay for the wall.

The wall must list the names of members of the United States Armed Forces who died in the Korean War. The Secretary of Defense sets who counts and sends a final list of names to the Secretary of the Interior. The wall may also show counts of those killed, wounded, or missing from the United States, Korean, and United Nations forces in that war.
plaw-114-231-2016:
Passed by the 114th Congress in 2016, Public Law 114-231 is the Eliminate, Neutralize, and Disrupt Wildlife Trafficking Act of 2016. The act backs world work against poaching. It aims to help partner nations fight the trade in wildlife and to name the worst nations for that trade.

The contents show five titles. Early titles state aims and United States policy, and call for a report on major wildlife trafficking countries. A third title sets a frame for joint agency work through a presidential task force. Later titles cover anti-poaching work, anti-trafficking work, work by United States missions abroad, and aid for local groups that guard wildlife.
plaw-114-232-2016:
Nevada Native Nations Land Act is the short title of Public Law 114-232, passed in 2016. In this act, the 114th Congress tells the Secretary of the Interior to take land into trust for some Indian tribes in Nevada. Land held in trust is held by the United States for a tribe's benefit.

One part shown covers the Fort McDermitt Paiute and Shoshone Tribe. About 19,094 acres run by the Bureau of Land Management, shown on a 2013 map as expansion lands, are held in trust for the tribe. That land becomes part of the tribe's reservation. A next part begins the same kind of transfer for the Shoshone Paiute Tribes.
plaw-114-233-2016: Public Law 114-233, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, makes one short change to an older law. The act amends the Gullah/Geechee Cultural Heritage Act. That act set up the Gullah/Geechee Cultural Heritage Corridor Commission. The change strikes the words 10 years in the old text and puts in 15 years. In effect, the life of the commission is stretched from ten years to fifteen years.
plaw-114-234-2016: Public Law 114-234, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, names a courthouse in North Carolina. The building stands at 150 Reade Circle in Greenville. While the building serves as a United States courthouse, it is known as the Randy D. Doub United States Courthouse. Any mention of that building in a law, map, rule, or other federal record during that time counts as a mention of it under that name.
plaw-114-235-2016:
Congress called Public Law 114-235 the Bathrooms Accessible in Every Situation Act, or BABIES Act. Passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, the act changes title 40 law on public buildings. Its aim is to put baby changing sites in restrooms in those buildings.

The new rule says restrooms in a public building must have baby changing sites that are safe, clean, and fit for use. The act lists cases where the rule does not apply. Those cases cover restrooms not open to the public, and restrooms where a sign points to a restroom with a changing table on the same floor. Cost and build limits can also excuse a site.
plaw-114-236-2016:
Survivors' Bill of Rights Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-236, passed by the 114th Congress. The act sets clear rights for people who have faced sexual assault. It adds a new chapter on those rights to title 18 of the United States Code.

The rights listed start with care and proof. A survivor may get a medical forensic exam and may not be blocked from it or charged for it. A survivor may also have the proof kit, or its key parts, kept at no charge for the legal time limit or 20 years, whichever is shorter. The act also gives a right to learn the results of the kit, such as a DNA match, when that does not harm a probe.
plaw-114-237-2016: Public Law 114-237, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, is the Clarification of Treatment of Electronic Sales of Livestock Act of 2016. The act amends the Packers and Stockyards Act of 1921. It widens the term market agency to cover a person who buys or sells livestock for a fee through online, video, or other electronic means. It reaches that person when the person handles the money from such sales, and the yearly sales pass a set threshold amount. The act also makes small wording fixes in the same section.
plaw-114-238-2016: Public Law 114-238, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, makes one narrow change to title 49 law. The change concerns grant pledges tied to airports. It adds a rule that an airport owner who renews a covered lease does not break a written pledge by that renewal alone. A covered lease must predate the act, charge a nominal rent, and have a federal or state body as tenant. It must also aid Air Force or Air National Guard flights at or from the airport.
plaw-114-239-2016:
United States Appreciation for Olympians and Paralympians Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-239. Passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, the act changes the tax code. It keeps Olympic and Paralympic prizes out of taxable income.

Under the new rule, gross income does not count the value of a medal won in the Olympic Games or Paralympic Games. It also does not count prize money paid by the United States Olympic Committee for such contests. The break does not apply when a person's adjusted gross income for the year passes a high limit set in the text. The change covers prizes and awards gained after December 31, 2015.
plaw-114-240-2016: Public Law 114-240 of 2016 is the Veterans Day Moment of Silence Act. The act changes title 36 law. It asks the President to issue a call each year for two minutes of silence on Veterans Day. The silence honors the service and loss of veterans through the nation's past. The act sets one shared start time, given hour by hour for each time zone from the Atlantic zone to the Hawaii-Aleutian zone.
plaw-114-241-2016: Treatment of Certain Payments in Eugenics Compensation Act is Public Law 114-241, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The act deals with cash paid by a state to people who were sterilized under state power in the past. It says such cash must not count as income or assets when a federal agency checks if a person can get a federal public benefit, or how much that benefit should be. The act then defines both of those key terms in full.
plaw-114-242-2016:
Federal Aviation Administration Veteran Transition Improvement Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-242. Passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, the act adds disabled veteran leave to the staff system of the Federal Aviation Administration, the agency that runs United States air travel.

The act ties the leave to a proof rule. A worker who uses the leave to get care for a wound or harm from service must give a signed note to the agency's human resource chief. The note must confirm the leave was used for that care, in the form the agency head sets. The change covers staff hired on or after a start date named later in the text.
plaw-114-243-2016: Passed in 2016, Public Law 114-243 renames a clinic for veterans in Colorado. The clinic is the community-based outpatient clinic of the Department of Veterans Affairs in Pueblo, Colorado. After the act took effect, the clinic is known as the PFC James Dunn VA Clinic. Any mention of that clinic in a law, rule, map, or other federal record counts as a mention of the clinic under its new name.
plaw-114-244-2016:
Alyce Spotted Bear and Walter Soboleff Commission on Native Children Act is Public Law 114-244, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress used the act to set up a named commission on Native children. The sample ends just as that step begins, so the duties of the group are not shown here.

Most of the sample gives the terms the act will use. A Native child means an Indian child, an Indian aged 18 to 24, or a Native Hawaiian not older than 24. The act also defines Indian, Indian tribe, and tribal college or university by pointing to older laws, and names the Secretary of the Interior as the Secretary in the act.
plaw-114-245-2016:
National Forest System Trails Stewardship Act, Public Law 114-245, was passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The act tells the Secretary of Agriculture to print a plan in the Federal Register. The plan must greatly raise the role of unpaid helpers and partners in care of trails in the National Forest System.

Findings state the scale of the task. The system holds more than 157,000 miles of trails for hiking, riding, hunting, bikes, and motor use. Congress finds the Forest Service can keep only about one quarter of trails to its own standard. It cites a repair backlog in the hundreds of millions of dollars. The contents add a first-choice trail care program, joint deals, and care credits for outfitters and guides.
plaw-114-246-2016: In 2016, the 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-246, which is the Gold Star Families Voices Act. The act amends the Veterans' Oral History Project Act. It lets that project gather video and audio accounts of the life stories of service members who went missing in action or died from their service in a time of war. Close family may tell those accounts. The act defines close family as a parent, spouse, sibling, or child.
plaw-114-247-2016:
No Veterans Crisis Line Call Should Go Unanswered Act is the title of Public Law 114-247, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress told the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to improve the Veterans Crisis Line, a phone and text help line for veterans in crisis.

The act orders two linked steps. First, the Secretary must write a quality guide with clear, scored goals for how fast and how well the line, and its backup call centers, reply. Second, the Secretary must make a plan so each call, text, and other contact is answered in time by a person. The plan must add tests of the line each fiscal year to find and fix faults.
plaw-114-248-2016: The 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-248 in 2016, and it makes a focused change to title 49 law. When the air agency weighs a project that may affect air travel, it must now weigh the effect on commercial space launch and return work as well. The added factor covers craft that arrive at or leave from a licensed launch or return site. The act gives the head of the Federal Aviation Administration 18 months to start a rule to put the change in place.
plaw-114-249-2016:
Outdoor Recreation Jobs and Economic Impact Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-249, passed by the 114th Congress. The act orders a study of the outdoor recreation economy of the United States. It asks what that economy adds to the whole United States economy.

The Secretary of Commerce must run the study with the farm and interior chiefs, through the Bureau of Economic Analysis. The study may weigh jobs, sales, and gains for travel and tourism. The Secretary must ask federal agencies and firms, small firms among them, for their views. A report of the results is due to Congress no later than two years after the act.
plaw-114-250-2016: Public Law 114-250 of 2016 changes title 5 law on extra pay. The act expands law enforcement availability pay, a form of added pay for staff who must stay on call. The old text covered a pilot with the customs service. The new text covers any staff member of the Air and Marine Operations arm of United States Customs and Border Protection, or a successor body. The change starts with the first pay period beginning at least 14 days after the act.
plaw-114-251-2016: Passed in 2016, Public Law 114-251 changes title 5 law on a pay top-up for retired air traffic controllers. Read closely, the act does not grant a new top-up. It states that the top-up section does not apply to a named group. That group is a person who left the job and then works full time as an air traffic control teacher. The work is under contract with the Federal Aviation Administration, at a site such as an airport.
plaw-114-252-2016: In 2016, the 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-252, which names a federal site in Texas. The site is the federal building and United States courthouse at 511 East San Antonio Avenue in El Paso, Texas. Under the act, the site is known as the R.E. Thomason Federal Building and United States Courthouse. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of it under that name.
plaw-114-253-2016: The 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-253 in 2016, and it names a federal site in Louisiana. The site is the federal building and United States courthouse at 300 Fannin Street in Shreveport, Louisiana. Under the act, the site is known as the Tom Stagg United States Court House, with Court House written as two words. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of it under that name.
plaw-114-254-2016:
In 2016, Public Law 114-254 was passed by the 114th Congress. It Carries the short title Further Continuing and Security Assistance Appropriations Act, 2017.
