That title differs from the catalog title, which speaks of energy and water funds for the year that ended September 30, 2016. The enacted text is the guide here.

The contents list two divisions. Division A is a further stopgap funds act for 2017. Division B is a security aid funds act for 2017, with titles for the defense and state agencies and for foreign work. The act also sets when funds may be used. Sums marked as urgent needs, or for war costs abroad, open only after the President marks them as such and tells Congress.
plaw-114-255-2016:
21st Century Cures Act is the short title of Public Law 114-255, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The act aims to speed the search for, the making of, and the delivery of new cures. It is a large health law with many parts.

The contents for Division A show the range. Early titles fund new work at the health research agency and the drug agency, and set up an account for state fights against opioid abuse. Later titles renew the health research agency, back exact-fit medicine aimed at each patient's traits, guard the privacy of people in studies, and help young scientists start their work.
plaw-114-256-2016:
Veterans Mobility Safety Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-256, passed by the 114th Congress. The act amends title 38 law to improve how the Department of Veterans Affairs gives cars and gear that adapts cars for veterans who need them.

One clause guards personal choice. The Secretary must make sure, as far as can be done, that a veteran who gets a car under the program may pick features of that car. A second clause orders a full policy on quality for firms that fit the gear. The policy must cover how the program is run, safety and quality norms for gear and fitting, and even use of those norms across the agency.
plaw-114-257-2016:
District of Columbia Judicial Financial Transparency Act is Public Law 114-257, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress wrote the act to update the money reports that judges of the District of Columbia courts must file. The act also makes other fixes to those courts.

The new text requires each judge to file a report at least once a year with the named commission. The report must give the source, kind, and sum of the judge's income above a low threshold, with like facts for a spouse's income above a higher threshold. It must also sort gains from rents, interest, and stock-type gains into set value bands.
plaw-114-258-2016:
Consumer Review Fairness Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-258, passed by the 114th Congress. The act bars some clauses in standard form contracts. Those clauses had blocked buyers from speaking or writing about the goods or services they bought in trade across state lines.

The act first defines its terms. A covered note can be a written, spoken, or picture review, or a like rating of goods, services, or conduct. A form contract is a contract with set terms that a buyer cannot truly debate, though job contracts are left out. The act then states that a clause in such a contract that blocks reviews is void from the start, save for named cases.
plaw-114-259-2016: Public Law 114-259 of 2016 names a lodging site for veterans in Indiana. The site is the temporary lodging facility of the Department of Veterans Affairs in Indianapolis, Indiana. After the act took effect, the site is known as the Dr. Otis Bowen Veteran House. Any mention of that site in a law, rule, map, or other federal record counts as a mention of the site under its new name.
plaw-114-260-2016: In 2016, the 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-260, which is the GAO Civilian Task and Delivery Order Protest Authority Act of 2016. The whole act does one thing. It strikes one paragraph from section 4106 of title 41 law. That paragraph held an end date for the right to protest a task or delivery order with the Government Accountability Office on civilian agency contracts. Striking it lifts that end date.
plaw-114-261-2016:
The 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-261 in 2016, and it strengthens guards for whistleblowers who work for federal contractors and grantees. A whistleblower is a worker who reports wrongdoing. The act guards such workers from being punished for their reports.

The text widens who is covered. For defense grants and for civilian grants, it adds staff of subgrantees and of personal services contractors to the shield. It also makes a pilot shield for contractor staff into a lasting one, by striking the pilot end clause. A further part bars paying back legal fees spent to fight a claim of such punishment, with the ban widened to subcontractors as well.
plaw-114-262-2016:
In 2016, Public Law 114-262 was passed by the 114th Congress. It Adds land to the reservation of the Siletz Tribe in Oregon. Its stated aim is to ease fee-to-trust requests for the tribe in a set area. Fee-to-trust means land a tribe owns is taken into trust by the United States.

The act lets the Secretary take title to more acres for the tribe. The land must lie inside the bounds of the first Siletz Coast Reservation of 1855, in six named Oregon counties. Land taken this way is held in trust for the tribe, counts as on-reservation land under the trust rules, and becomes part of the tribe's reservation.
plaw-114-263-2016:
Public Law 114-263 of 2016 amends the Grand Ronde Reservation Act. The catalog calls the changes technical fixes, and the act's own heading speaks of added land for the Grand Ronde Reservation in Oregon.

The text lets the Secretary take title to more real property for the Tribes. The land must lie inside the bounds of their first reservation of 1857, in Polk and Yamhill Counties, Oregon. It must be given to the United States by or for the Tribes. A request to take such land into trust is treated as an on-reservation request. The sample then turns to a clause on gaming, where it is cut off.
plaw-114-264-2016:
Program Management Improvement Accountability Act is Public Law 114-264, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress amended title 31 law to set up posts and bodies that improve how federal agencies run programs and projects.

The act gives new duties to the Deputy Director for Management. That officer must set shared norms, rules, and guides for program and project work across agencies, and watch how they are used. The officer must chair a new Program Management Policy Council. Other duties shown are to set norms drawn from widely used practice, seek best practice from private firms, and review groups of programs flagged as high risk by the Government Accountability Office.
plaw-114-265-2016:
Filipino Veterans of World War II Congressional Gold Medal Act of 2015 is Public Law 114-265, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress voted to award a Congressional Gold Medal as a group to Filipino veterans of World War II. The award honors their devoted service in that war.

Long findings trace the shared past. They recall that Filipinos declared their land free on June 12, 1898, yet the Treaty of Paris gave control to the United States for a large cash sum. They note that Filipino troops joined the United States Army as the Philippine Scouts in 1901. They also note a 1934 law set a path to end colonial rule, while the United States kept the right to call Filipinos to serve until freedom came in 1946.
plaw-114-266-2016:
Passed in 2016, Public Law 114-266 orders a joint plan against Boko Haram. The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense must write the plan together. It must be sent to the right groups in Congress within 180 days.

The plan must run five years. It must help the Government of Nigeria, the joint task force formed to fight Boko Haram, and other partners beat the threat in their region. It must also help Nigeria and its neighbors hear the fair complaints of weak groups in the zones the group harms. Parts shown cover stronger local forces, aid for civilians hurt by the group, and steps to probe abuse by security forces.
plaw-114-267-2016:
Northern Border Security Review Act is the short title of Public Law 114-267, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress told the Secretary of Homeland Security to study threats at the northern border. In the act, that border means the land and sea borders between the United States and Canada.

The study is due within 180 days to six named groups in Congress. It must cover current and future terror and crime threats from people and gangs who seek to enter the United States through that border, or to use weak spots there. It must also cover what fixes are needed at and between the ports where people cross.
plaw-114-268-2016:
First Responder Anthrax Preparedness Act is Public Law 114-268, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The act tells the Secretary of Homeland Security to make anthrax vaccines open to emergency response staff. Anthrax is a grave disease that could be used in an attack.

The act sets up a pilot program run with the health chief. States may give the shots to response staff who face high risk if an attack comes, and who agree to take them of their own free will. The shots come from the national stockpile and must be near the end of their marked use dates. The health chief must first find that a batch is not set aside for other needs and that its use will not hurt care in a health crisis.
plaw-114-269-2016:
Office of Strategic Services Congressional Gold Medal Act is Public Law 114-269, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress voted to award the Congressional Gold Medal as a group to the members of the Office of Strategic Services, called the OSS. The award honors their top service and large role in World War II.

Findings call the OSS the first United States bid to build a system of spying in that war. They say it laid the base for the modern spy and special operations groups of the United States. They name its founder, General William J. Donovan, as the sole person in United States past to win the nation's four top honors. They also trace today's special forces, Navy SEALs, and Army groups back to OSS units.
plaw-114-270-2016:
Expanding Capacity for Health Outcomes Act, or ECHO Act, is Public Law 114-270, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress ordered studies and reports on a health teaching model. The model uses live video links to join experts with many other health staff at once for case-based learning.

Most of the sample defines the terms the studies will use. A health staff shortage area and a zone or group with too little care are defined by their marks in older health law. The model itself is defined as a distance health teaching setup. Through linked video, experts train and guide local staff so care can improve in the places the act names.
plaw-114-271-2016: In 2016, the 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-271, which guards funds for the National Human Trafficking Hotline. It strikes a clause in the Trafficking Victims Protection Act that had tied hotline grants to funds set aside for other grants. The act also fixes a wording slip in the Justice for Victims of Trafficking Act of 2015, changing one phrase to read Victims of Trafficking. Both changes count as if passed with that 2015 act.
plaw-114-272-2016: The 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-272 in 2016, and it is the Daniel J. Evans Olympic National Park Wilderness Act. The act gives a new name to wild land in Washington. It strikes the words Olympic Wilderness in the Washington Park Wilderness Act of 1988 and puts in Daniel J. Evans Wilderness. Any mention of the Olympic Wilderness in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the land under its new name.
plaw-114-273-2016: Charles Duncan Buried with Honor Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-273, passed by the 114th Congress. The act changes title 38 law on burial help for veterans. It lets the Secretary of Veterans Affairs supply caskets and urns for a veteran who has no next of kin or lacks the means to pay for them. The help now covers burial in a veterans cemetery of a state or tribal group that got a federal grant for that cemetery, not only in a national cemetery.
plaw-114-274-2016:
Better Online Ticket Sales Act of 2016, or BOTS Act of 2016, is Public Law 114-274. Passed by the 114th Congress, the act bars tricks that dodge the controls web ticket sellers use. Those controls aim to give all buyers a fair shot at tickets for an event.

The ban has two prongs. A person may not slip past a safety check, access control, or like tool that a ticket seller uses to hold purchase caps or guard order rules. A person also may not sell a ticket gained that way in trade across state lines, if that person took part in the dodge or knew of it. The act leaves room for probes, law work, and study of flaws in such tools.
plaw-114-275-2016: Prescribed Burn Approval Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-275, passed by the 114th Congress. A prescribed burn is a fire set on purpose as part of a plan. The act bars the Secretary of Agriculture from allowing such a burn on Forest Service land. The bar holds when the national fire danger scale reads extreme for that county or a county next to it. The Secretary may still allow the burn by working with the state and local fire chiefs. A yearly report to Congress must list the burns held.
plaw-114-276-2016: In 2016, Public Law 114-276 was passed by the 114th Congress. It Names a clinic for veterans in Michigan. The clinic is the Traverse City VA Community-Based Outpatient Clinic in Traverse City. Under the act, it is known as the Colonel Demas T. Craw VA Clinic. Findings in the act recall that Craw won the Medal of Honor for brave work in North Africa in 1942. He also won the Purple Heart and other awards, after he joined the Army in 1918.
plaw-114-277-2016: Iran Sanctions Extension Act is the short title of Public Law 114-277, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The act does one thing: it renews the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996. It strikes the end date of December 31, 2016 in that older act and puts in December 31, 2026. A note in the text adds that the act became law without the President's signature on December 15, 2016, after the time set by law for his reply ran out.
plaw-114-278-2016:
Public Law 114-278 of 2016 orders a full check of the transport worker security card program. The Secretary of Homeland Security must prep the review. The card gives named workers access to safe zones of ships and port sites.

First steps are due fast. Within 60 days, the head of the Transportation Security Administration must start work to improve how people with access are screened. The work shown covers a full risk study of the screening steps, a search for steps that need more checks, and use of the best methods found. It also covers better fraud checks, such as proof checks for papers and yearly training for trusted agents.
plaw-114-279-2016:
Cross-Border Trade Enhancement Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-279, passed by the 114th Congress. The act gives new ways to pay for services and for build work at land border ports of entry. It adds a part on joint work between the public and private sides to the Homeland Security Act.

Under the new part, the head of Customs and Border Protection may sign a fee deal at the plea of any party. The agency gives the named services at a port of entry or other site. The party pays a fee that covers the full cost of those services. If the party gives space, it must keep and equip the site at no cost to the federal government, to the agency's set norms.
plaw-114-280-2016: In 2016, the 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-280, which names a clinic for veterans in Ohio. Findings say Daniel L. Kinnard served as a medic with the 101st Airborne Division in Vietnam and won the Bronze Star for heroism under fire in 1968, plus the Purple Heart. He was killed in action that year while he gave aid to fellow troops. Under the act, the veterans clinic in Newark, Ohio, is known as the Daniel L. Kinnard VA Clinic.
plaw-114-281-2016:
Frank R. Wolf International Religious Freedom Act is Public Law 114-281, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress amended the International Religious Freedom Act of 1998. The aim is to help the United States push for freedom of faith around the world through talks, training, terror work, aid, and firmer replies to abuse.

The contents list three titles. Title I covers State Department work, such as its faith freedom office, its yearly report, training for Foreign Service staff, and lists of jailed people of faith. Title II puts a special adviser on faith freedom at the National Security Council. Title III covers acts by the President, such as naming non-state groups that abuse faith and replies to the worst abuse.
plaw-114-282-2016:
Apollo 11 50th Anniversary Commemorative Coin Act is Public Law 114-282, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress told the Secretary of the Treasury to mint special coins. The coins mark 50 years since the first crewed landing on the Moon.

Findings recall the flight. Apollo 11 left Florida on July 16, 1969, with Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins aboard. The crew made the first steps on the Moon on July 20, 1969. Congress finds the United States is the sole land to have landed people on a body off Earth and brought them home safe. The findings quote President John F. Kennedy's 1962 pledge to go to the Moon in that decade, hard as the task was.
plaw-114-283-2016: The 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-283 in 2016, and it names a post office site in California. The site is the United States Postal Service site at 1221 State Street, Suite 12, in Santa Barbara, California. The catalog title drops the word to before designate, but the enacted text is clear. Under the act, the site is known by a long name that honors a Navy SEAL master chief petty officer, Louis Lou J. Langlais. Mentions of the site in federal records count under that name.
plaw-114-284-2016:
SEC Small Business Advocate Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-284, passed by the 114th Congress. The act amends the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It sets up two new bodies at the market watch agency to aid small firms that seek funds.

One body is an office led by an Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation. That chief reports straight to the Commission and is picked from people with a past of work for small firms and their funding. A current staff member of the agency may not take the post. The pay is set at the top rate for senior staff who report to the Commission. The act also sets up an advice group on small firm funding.
plaw-114-285-2016:
Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers Reform and Improvement Act of 2015 is Public Law 114-285, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress rewrote the law on the Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers, known as FLETC. The centers train first responders and law staff, for homeland safety and terror response work.

The new text keeps FLETC in the homeland agency, led by a Director who reports to the Secretary. The Director must set training goals and plans, run the sites and courses, and build course plans for federal, state, local, tribal, and world law and safety staff. Those plans cover home readiness and replies to threats or acts of terror. The Director must also track how well the plans and sites work.
plaw-114-286-2016:
Faster Care for Veterans Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-286, passed by the 114th Congress. The act tells the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to run a pilot program. In the pilot, veterans book and confirm their own health visits through a web site or phone app at agency health sites.

The pilot must start within 120 days. The Secretary must pick at least three of the agency's service zones for the test. The Secretary must seek a deal, through an open contest, with a firm that sells a ready-made self-booking system. A call for bids is due within 60 days, and a deal must be signed within 120 days of the act.
plaw-114-287-2016:
Federal Assets Sale and Transfer Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-287, passed by the 114th Congress. The act aims to cut the deficit by joining and selling federal buildings and other civilian land the government no longer needs.

The contents show a board-led plan. Early parts set up a board, its meets, pay, chief, staff, and deal powers. Later parts cover how tips reach the board, the board's duties, review by the budget office, and how the sales are done. Other parts cover a real property data file and a review by the Government Accountability Office. They also cover a share of sale cash kept by agencies, and named sales of two sites in the capital area.
plaw-114-288-2016: In 2016, Public Law 114-288 was passed by the 114th Congress. It Assigns a name to a federal site in Georgia. The site, at 121 Spring Street SE in Gainesville, serves as both a federal building and a United States courthouse. Congress directed that it be called the Sidney Oslin Smith, Jr. Federal Building and United States Courthouse. Federal laws, maps, and records that point to that site are read as pointing to it under the new name.
plaw-114-289-2016:
National Park Service Centennial Act is Public Law 114-289, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The act readies the National Park Service for its 100th year in 2016. It also looks to a second century of care for the natural, past, and cultural wealth of the national parks, for guests now and in years to come.

The contents list four titles. Title I sets up a National Park Centennial Challenge Fund and a like pass price for seniors. Title II creates a Second Century fund for the service, held through the National Park Foundation. Title III covers teaching in the parks, the Public Land Corps, and park helpers who give their time. Title IV deals with the board and funds of the foundation.
plaw-114-290-2016: In Shelby, Indiana, a postal site gains a name under Public Law 114-290, passed in 2016. Congress acted through the 114th Congress. The site stands at 23323 Shelby Road. From the act on, it carries the name Richard Allen Cable Post Office. A mention of the Shelby Road site in any federal law, map, or file is treated as a mention of the Richard Allen Cable Post Office.
plaw-114-291-2016:
United States-Caribbean Strategic Engagement Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-291, passed by the 114th Congress. The act seeks closer ties with the states of the Caribbean region. It also seeks closer ties with Caribbean people who live in the United States, and with firms and civic groups on both sides.

Congress states a nine-point policy. The points call for warmer ties, more trade work, and aid for joint growth in the region. They call for lasting growth, more types of trade, and a stronger place in world trade. They also call for less crime and drug trade, a stronger rule of law, and safer power from more sources. They call for joint work on rights at world meets, more health work, and wider web access. A joint plan from the State chief is due within 180 days.
plaw-114-292-2016:
Combat-Injured Veterans Tax Fairness Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-292, passed by the 114th Congress. The act aims to give back sums wrongly held for tax from severance pay. The pay went to troops who left service with wounds from combat.

Findings give the scale. Each year about 10,000 to 11,000 people leave the Armed Forces for health reasons, and some of them leave with combat wounds. Congress had kept severance pay for such wounds free of tax. Yet since 1991, the findings say, the Defense chief held tax from that pay in error. Many who are owed funds can no longer file a fixed tax form in time. The act orders the Defense chief to find the flawed payments within one year, where the sample ends.
plaw-114-293-2016: Passed in 2016, Public Law 114-293 is the Bottles and Breastfeeding Equipment Screening Act. Within 90 days, the head of the Transportation Security Administration must tell airlines and screeners what the agency's own guides say. The guides let baby formula, breast milk, clean water for infants, and juice be carried on planes as a named break from the liquids rule. Screeners must also get training on the special checks for such items.
plaw-114-294-2016:
Communities Helping Invest through Property and Improvements Needed for Veterans Act of 2016 is a long name for Public Law 114-294. People also call it the CHIP IN for Vets Act of 2016. The 114th Congress passed it in 2016 to test joint deals that build new sites for the Department of Veterans Affairs.

Under the pilot, the Secretary may take gifts of land and sites from named givers. A gift may be land with a built site, land for a site the giver will build, or a site built on agency land. Givers may be a state or local body, a tax-free charity group, a limited firm, a private party, or a donor or donor group.
plaw-114-295-2016: Staten Island gains a named postal building under Public Law 114-295, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The building sits at 3031 Veterans Road West in Staten Island, New York. Congress gave it the name Leonard Montalto Post Office Building. When a federal law, map, rule, or file speaks of that Veterans Road West site, the words are read as the Leonard Montalto Post Office Building.
plaw-114-296-2016: Public Law 114-296, from the 114th Congress in 2016, honors an Army officer in the name of a postal building in Mississippi. You will find the building at 401 McElroy Drive in Oxford. Its formal name under the act is the Army First Lieutenant Donald C. Carwile Post Office Building. Any federal record that names the McElroy Drive site names the Carwile building.
plaw-114-297-2016: A Texas postal site takes a personal name in Public Law 114-297, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress chose the site at 14231 TX-150 in Coldspring, Texas. It is now the E. Marie Youngblood Post Office. References to the Coldspring site in laws, maps, rules, or other records of the United States are deemed references to the E. Marie Youngblood Post Office.
plaw-114-298-2016: In 2016, the 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-298, which gives a group honor in Zapata, Texas. The postal site at 810 N US Highway 83 in Zapata is called the Zapata Veterans Post Office under the act. The name honors veterans as a group rather than one person. A law, map, or record that cites the Highway 83 site cites the Zapata Veterans Post Office.
plaw-114-299-2016: Marietta, Georgia, is the home of the postal site named by Public Law 114-299, passed in 2016. The site stands at 2886 Sandy Plains Road. Congress, in the 114th Congress, called it the Marine Lance Corporal Squire Skip Wells Post Office Building, with Skip set off in quotes in the text. Federal records that mention the Sandy Plains Road site are read as mentions of the Wells building.
plaw-114-300-2016: Chicago's postal map changes under Public Law 114-300, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The site at 6300 N. Northwest Highway in Chicago, Illinois, is the site in question. Congress named it the Officer Joseph P. Cali Post Office Building. In a law, map, rule, or other United States record, a citation of the Northwest Highway site counts as a citation of the Cali building.
plaw-114-301-2016:
GAO Mandates Revision Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-301, passed by the 114th Congress. GAO is the Government Accountability Office, the audit arm of Congress. The act cuts or changes some of the reports and duties that older laws had laid on that office.

One part cuts named reports in full. It strikes a Single Audit Act watch duty and shifts the next section's number. It ends a review of Medigap premium levels, a report on a disaster claim pilot, and a two-year survey on transport reports. A next part then changes other reports rather than ending them, starting with watch and audit work under the 2008 bank rescue law.
plaw-114-302-2016:
Federal Bureau of Investigation Whistleblower Protection Enhancement Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-302. Passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress, the act aims to give sound guards to whistleblowers at the Federal Bureau of Investigation. A whistleblower reports wrongdoing and can face harm at work for doing so.

The act rewrites the ban on bad staff acts at the Bureau. It bars acts taken as payback for a report of facts. A staff member may report to a boss in the direct chain of command, up to the agency head. Other safe paths are the Inspector General and the ethics offices of the Justice agency and the Bureau. They also include its Inspection Division, the Office of Special Counsel, or a person named to take such reports.
plaw-114-303-2016: Public Law 114-303, passed in 2016, names a postal building in Evanston, Illinois. The 114th Congress picked the site at 1101 Davis Street in Evanston. That site now bears the name Abner J. Mikva Post Office Building. If a federal law, map, rule, or paper points to the Davis Street site, it points to the Mikva building.
plaw-114-304-2016:
United States-Israel Advanced Research Partnership Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-304, passed by the 114th Congress. The act amends two older laws, the Homeland Security Act of 2002 and the United States-Israel Strategic Partnership Act of 2014. Its aim is joint homeland research and anti-terror work, with a focus on cyber safety.

The changes add report duties first. Reports must update the state of joint work named in the prior report, say if goals were met, share lessons, and judge the work as a whole. They must also tell what blocks got in the way, such as office, legal, or talks-based blocks, or a lack of funds. A new part then lets a named chief, with the State agency, join joint cyber research work.
plaw-114-305-2016: Saipan holds the postal site named by Public Law 114-305, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. Find it at 1 Chalan Kanoa VLG in Saipan, Northern Mariana Islands. The act calls it the Segundo T. Sablan and CNMI Fallen Military Heroes Post Office Building. The name joins one man, Segundo T. Sablan, with the fallen service heroes of the islands, marked CNMI in the text. Records that cite the Saipan site cite that building.
plaw-114-306-2016: Public Law 114-306, passed in 2016, assigns a name to a postal building in Chula Vista, California. The building is at 830 Kuhn Drive. Congress, in the 114th Congress, designated it the Jonathan J.D. De Guzman Post Office Building, with the initials in quotes in the text. A reference in a law, map, or other United States record to the Kuhn Drive site is a reference to the De Guzman building.
plaw-114-307-2016: Public Law 114-307 of 2016 concerns deals for airport work. The head of the Federal Aviation Administration may sign a paid-back deal with a state or local agency. In such a deal, the agency pays the costs back. The deal must cover a project at an airport where notice is required under a named flight rule. Two guards apply: the deal must hold steps for low-cost, sound work, and it must not harm the safety or smooth flow of the national air system.
plaw-114-308-2016:
Holocaust Expropriated Art Recovery Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-308, passed by the 114th Congress. The act seeks to give victims of Holocaust-era abuse, and their heirs, a fair chance to win back art. The art was seized or taken by the Nazis.

Findings state the scale of the theft. The Nazis seized or took hundreds of thousands of works of art and other goods across Europe, as part of their murder drive against the Jewish people and other groups. After World War II, the United States and its allies tried to send the art back to its lands of origin. Many works were never joined with their owners, and some have since been found in the United States.
plaw-114-309-2016: Port Hueneme, California, holds the postal site named by Public Law 114-309, passed in 2016. Look for it at 560 East Pleasant Valley Road, Port Hueneme. The 114th Congress called the site the U.S. Naval Construction Battalion Seabees Fallen Heroes Post Office Building, with Seabees in quotes in the text. The name honors fallen members of the Navy build crews. A federal record that names the Pleasant Valley Road site names that building.
plaw-114-310-2016: Bronx, New York, holds the postal building named by Public Law 114-310, passed in 2016. You will find it at 2024 Jerome Avenue in the Bronx. The 114th Congress designated it the Dr. Roscoe C. Brown, Jr. Post Office Building. A citation of the Jerome Avenue site in a law, map, rule, or other United States record is a citation of the Brown building.
plaw-114-311-2016: Overtime Pay for Protective Services Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-311, passed by the 114th Congress. The act raises extra pay for guard work in 2016. A covered worker is any officer, staff, or agent of the United States Secret Service who guards a person or event the service protects in 2016. For such staff, the normal cap on extra pay in title 5 law does not apply in 2016 as stated in the act. Extra pay paid under the break does not count as basic pay.
plaw-114-312-2016: Public Law 114-312 of 2016 names a postal site in Florence, Arizona. The site stands at 501 North Main Street in Florence. Its name under the act is the Adolfo Harpo Celaya Post Office, with Harpo in quotes in the text. When a federal law, map, or record names the Main Street site, it names the Celaya post office.
plaw-114-313-2016: Passed in 2016, Public Law 114-313 names a health system for veterans in California. The system is at 5901 East 7th Street in Long Beach, California. After the act, the system is known as the Tibor Rubin VA Medical Center. Any mention of that health system in a law, rule, map, or other federal paper counts as a mention of the Tibor Rubin VA Medical Center.
plaw-114-314-2016: In 2016, the 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-314, which resets the lines of some coastal units in New Jersey. The units sit in the John H. Chafee Coastal Barrier Resources System. The act swaps out a map dated August 1, 2014 for three named units. A new map dated October 7, 2016 takes its place and adds two more units, Sayreville and Matawan Point. The Secretary of the Interior must keep the new map on file for public viewing.
plaw-114-315-2016:
Jeff Miller and Richard Blumenthal Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvement Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-315. Passed by the 114th Congress, the act amends title 38 law. It makes a set of fixes to the laws run by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.

Title I, as listed, covers pay for harm from service. It speeds pay of survivor benefits and lets the appeals board hold video hearings. It makes the Secretary print the mean time to judge early and late appeals. It also orders a review of how area offices handle claims, a report on staff levels under the national work queue, and facts on claim capacity in the yearly budget plea.
plaw-114-316-2016: Promoting Travel, Commerce, and National Security Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-316, passed by the 114th Congress. The act does one narrow job. It keeps United States court power over crimes by United States staff posted in Canada for border safety work. A covered person works for the homeland or justice agency, as staff or contractor, and is in Canada under a treaty or deal. Conduct in Canada that would be a crime in the United States is fined or jailed as for that crime.
plaw-114-317-2016:
Inspector General Empowerment Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-317, passed by the 114th Congress. The act amends the Inspector General Act of 1978. Its aim is to strengthen the free hand of the Inspectors General, the watchdogs inside federal agencies.

The contents list eight parts. Early parts add powers for the watchdogs and add duties for their joint council. Later parts cover reports and added facts, and full and fast access to all papers. One part covers access to facts for some named watchdogs. The act ends with small wording fixes and a bar on new funds under the act.
plaw-114-318-2016:
Federal Property Management Reform Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-318, passed by the 114th Congress. The act aims to improve how the whole federal government runs its property. Property here means land, buildings, and like assets the government holds.

The stated purpose has three prongs. First, the Postal Service must take fit steps to run and count its property with more care. Second, the act backs more shared use of space with postal sites, and gives guides on how the Postal Service leases space. Third, it sets up a Federal Real Property Council. That council must write guides and make sure plans for better care of federal property are carried out.
plaw-114-319-2016:
Foreign Cultural Exchange Jurisdictional Immunity Clarification Act is Public Law 114-319, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress amended chapter 97 of title 28 law. The change clears up when a foreign state can be sued in a United States court over art on loan for a show.

The new rule shields loan shows that meet three tests. A work must come into the United States from a foreign state under a deal for a short show, with that state as owner or keeper. The President, or a named stand-in, must find the work holds cultural weight and the show serves the national good. Notice of that finding must be printed as an older law requires. Work tied to such a show is then not trade work by that state.
plaw-114-320-2016: The 114th Congress passed Public Law 114-320 in 2016, and it approves a nuclear deal with Norway. The deal is the Agreement for Cooperation Between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Kingdom of Norway Concerning Peaceful Uses of Nuclear Energy. It was done at Washington on June 11, 2016. The act lets the deal take effect at once, as if all review steps in the Atomic Energy Act had been met. Once in effect, it stays under that act and other United States law.
plaw-114-321-2016:
RESPONSE Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-321, passed by the 114th Congress. RESPONSE stands for Railroad Emergency Services Preparedness, Operational Needs, and Safety Evaluation. The act sets up a RESPONSE group under the National Advisory Council of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

The group must give tips on training and gear for responders who face hazardous goods crashes that involve railroads. The agency head must form the group within 30 days. Members shown are drawn from the emergency agency, from the pipeline and hazardous goods safety agency, and from the homeland agency's emergency talk office, or their named stand-ins.
plaw-114-322-2016:
Water Infrastructure Improvements for the Nation Act, or WIIN Act, is Public Law 114-322, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress wrote the act to improve the rivers and harbors of the United States. It also backs care and growth of water and linked resources.

Title I covers water work. Its first subtitle lists general parts shown in the sample. They cover youth service and nature corps groups, safe travel by boat, new harbors, federal breakwaters and jetties, and remote harbors where people live off local catch and goods. Other parts cover new ways to dredge, the Great Lakes travel system, funds to keep harbors in repair, donor ports, and deeper harbor work.
plaw-114-323-2016:
Department of State Authorities Act, Fiscal Year 2017 is Public Law 114-323, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The opening line says the act grants powers to the Department of State for fiscal year 2016, though the title names fiscal year 2017. The contents are the best guide to its scope.

Title I covers embassy safety and staff safety. One subtitle sets review and plan rules, such as marks for high risk, high threat posts and backup plans for them. A second subtitle covers site safety and staff rules, such as a shared cost plan for safe sites, local guard deals abroad, and safety boosts for soft targets. A third subtitle, on safety training, begins where the sample ends.
plaw-114-324-2016:
Justice for All Reauthorization Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-324, passed by the 114th Congress. The act lists wide aims in its opening lines. They cover crime victims' rights, the backlog of DNA and other proof samples, and test skill in federal, state, and local crime labs.

Other aims in the same lines are new test tools, new training on how proof is gathered and used, and DNA tests after a verdict to free the guiltless. The act also backs proof-lab standards, training and gear needs, and better work by lawyers in state death cases. One early clause shown lets a court order a wrongdoer to pay back a victim as a term of watch after jail.
plaw-114-325-2016:
Emmett Till Unsolved Civil Rights Crimes Reauthorization Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-325, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress renewed the Emmett Till Unsolved Civil Rights Crime Act of 2007. That older act drives probes of old, unsolved civil rights crimes.

The changes add duties to the probe work. Staff must meet with fit groups to share facts and talk through the state of the work. They must back a full count of all victims whose deaths or loss came from race-based crimes. They must hold to account, under federal and state law, those who did or helped such crimes. They must also give sympathy to the towns and families hit, keep families told of the probe's state, and grant fact requests fast, with one public store of the shared papers.
plaw-114-326-2016: National Urban Search and Rescue Response System Act of 2016 is Public Law 114-326, passed by the 114th Congress. The act grants legal power to a national city search and rescue system, run under the disaster aid law. Most of the sample defines the words of the new part. A sponsoring agency is a state or local body that backs a task force in the system. A participating agency joins by deal with a sponsor and may be a state or local body, a charity, or a private group.
plaw-114-327-2016:
Ensuring Access to Pacific Fisheries Act is Public Law 114-327, passed in 2016 by the 114th Congress. The act puts two sea pacts into United States law. One pact guards high seas fish stocks in the North Pacific Ocean. The other guards high seas fish stocks in the South Pacific Ocean.

Title I covers the North Pacific pact. Its first part defines the terms of the plan. The Commission is the North Pacific Fisheries Commission set up by the pact. A Commissioner is a United States member named under the act. The Convention Area is the zone the pact covers. Council means one of three named fishery councils under the main fishery law, as the facts require.
plaw-114-328-2016:
National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 is Public Law 114-328, passed in 2016. The 114th Congress used this large yearly act to grant funds for 2017. The funds cover armed work of the Department of Defense, army building, and defense work of the Department of Energy. The act also sets troop strength for that year.

The act is split into five divisions. Division A grants Department of Defense powers. Division B grants army building powers. Division C grants Department of Energy national safety powers and other powers. Division D holds the funding tables. Division E reforms the Uniform Code of Military Justice, the code of law for the armed forces.
plos-pbio-0020416:
Daniel Ortiz-Barrientos, Brian A. Counterman, and Mohamed A. F. Noor reviewed how new species can arise in PLOS Biology in 2004. Reinforcement is the idea that natural selection strengthens barriers between two groups when their hybrid offspring are unfit. Mating with the wrong group wastes effort, so traits that prevent it spread.

The review weighs genetic evidence for the process in nature. It sorts systems where reinforcement looks real from those where other causes fit better. The question is a live one in evolution, since it bears on how species stay distinct while living side by side. A clear-eyed summary like this one helps field workers design tests that can actually settle it.
plos-pone-0000016:
Yang Zhou, Hao Wu, Shuai Li, and co-authors reported in 2006 on a protein the brain needs to lock in lasting memories. Long-term potentiation is the lasting strengthening of a connection between nerve cells, and its late phase is what turns a fresh impression into a durable memory. The hippocampus, a deep brain structure, is central to that process.

The team showed that TORC1, a protein that helps switch on memory-related genes, is required for the late phase to hold in the hippocampus. Block that step, and the strengthening fades. The result connects memory storage to gene activity inside the cell, and it points at a control point that later memory research keeps returning to.
plos-pone-0000116:
Zhong Hua, Qing Lv, Wenbin Ye, and colleagues published this cell biology paper in PLOS ONE in 2006. It examines how tiny RNA molecules called microRNAs control VEGF and other angiogenic factors. These factors drive angiogenesis, the growth of new blood vessels, when oxygen runs low, a state called hypoxia.

Blood vessel growth feeds healing tissue, but it also feeds tumors. The authors trace how microRNAs adjust the levels of these vessel-promoting factors under low oxygen. The findings matter for cancer and eye disease research, where blocking or boosting this pathway could change how a disease progresses.
plos-pone-0000216:
Ning Fu, Ines Drinnenberg, and Janet Kelso published this comparative genomics paper in PLOS ONE in 2007. It compares humans and chimpanzees, asking how the evolution of proteins lines up with the evolution of the RNA messages that encode them. The authors measure both kinds of change across the two species.

Proteins and their messages do not always evolve at the same pace, and the mismatch is informative. The comparison shows where regulation, rather than protein change, drove differences between the species. That distinction matters for the long debate over what, genetically, makes humans different from our closest relatives.
plos-pone-0000316:
Màté A. Demény, Evi Soutoglou, Zita Nagy, and colleagues published this molecular biology paper in PLOS ONE in 2007. TAFs are parts of the machinery that starts transcription, the reading of genes. The authors identify a small TAF complex and describe its role in assembling the larger TAF-containing complexes that switch genes on.

Gene activation is built from modular parts that snap together in steps. A small sub-complex acting as an assembly piece clarifies that construction. The work refines the parts list of the transcription machinery, one of the most fundamental systems in the cell.
plos-pone-0000416:
Shih-Chieh Hung and colleagues tested whether a brief spell of low oxygen primes healing cells, in a 2007 PLOS ONE paper. The cells are multipotent stromal cells, versatile cells from marrow that can settle into damaged tissue. After short exposure to low oxygen, the team measured two surface receptors, CX3CR1 and CXCR4, and how well the cells engrafted in living tissue.

The authors report that low oxygen raised both receptors and improved engraftment in vivo. Receptors like these act as homing gear, helping cells find and enter injured sites. A simple preconditioning step that boosts homing could make cell therapies work better without genetic tinkering.
plos-pone-0000516:
Robert J. Greenstein and colleagues revisited two old drugs' action on a stubborn bacterium, in a 2007 PLOS ONE paper. The drugs are 5-amino-salicylic acid and its partner sulfapyridine, used for bowel inflammation. The target is M. avium including subspecies paratuberculosis, a slow-growing bacterium linked to Johne's disease in cattle and debated in Crohn's disease.

Whether these drugs act directly on the bacterium matters for how they help patients. It also matters for a contested claim. That claim holds that the bacterium drives some Crohn's cases. Laboratory action studies cannot settle the disease debate, but they clarify what the drugs do to the organism itself. The paper adds data to a long argument.
plos-pone-0000616:
Jan R.T. van Weering, Ruud F. Toonen and Matthijs Verhage wrote for PLOS ONE in 2007 about the final steps before a cell releases its cargo. Rab3a is a small protein that sits on secretory vesicles, the tiny sacs that carry chemicals out of the cell. It flips between an active form bound to GTP and an inactive form bound to GDP.

Docking, the vesicle's arrival and holding at the cell surface, is the step under study. The authors tested different Rab3a forms and gene combinations, drawing on yeast work where related genes interact. Their title states that docking needs Rab3a to bind and release its phosphate partners, plus the protein Munc18-1.
plos-pone-0000716:
John P. Grieco, Nicole L. Achee, Theeraphap Chareonviriyaphap and co-authors proposed a new way to sort the chemicals sprayed on walls against malaria mosquitoes. The method is called indoor residual spraying, or IRS. How mosquitoes respond to these chemicals is of great importance. It decides how well a spray blocks the spread of malaria.

A set of lab tests measured mosquito responses in hard numbers. Some chemicals kill on contact. Others drive mosquitoes away, or merely irritate them into leaving. The authors argue these actions should be classed apart, not lumped under one label. A clear scheme helps malaria programs pick the right product, and helps scientists compare studies that long used loose terms.
plos-pone-0000816:
Adrienne C. M. Persoon, Pieter L. Jager, Wim J. Sluiter and co-authors compared two ways to watch for the return of thyroid cancer. After treatment for this cancer, doctors track a protein called thyroglobulin, or Tg, in the blood. A rise can mean the cancer is back. A very sensitive Tg test can catch small rises. So can a test done after a dose of rhTSH, a lab-made hormone that pushes Tg up.

The team weighed the yield of both tests in long-term follow-up care. The hormone route means extra shots, cost, and side effects for the patient. If the sensitive test alone does as well, patients can skip all that. Head-to-head data like this give doctors a firm base for a choice they face at every check-up.
plos-pone-0000916:
Agnes Roure, Ute Rothbacher, Francois Robin and co-authors assembled a set of gateway vectors for embryo research, published in PLOS ONE in 2007. Genomic data, full length gene copies and control sequences have piled up for more and more species. Comparing protein function across species needs tools that move genes between test systems with little fuss.

Their multicassette vector set is built for high throughput work in Ciona, a small sea animal, and in vertebrate embryos. A shared toolkit lets researchers run the same gene in different embryos and compare fairly. That kind of comparison is how shared developmental rules get separated from species specific twists.
plos-pone-0001016:
Roland Meier, Annick Muhlethaler-Mottet, Marjorie Flahaut and colleagues studied a receptor that fuels neuroblastoma growth, in PLOS ONE in 2007. Neuroblastoma is a childhood cancer that varies widely and turns deadly in its higher stages. It tends to spread to the liver and bone marrow, and beyond surgery there was still no efficient treatment.

The receptor CXCR4, the team report, strongly promotes both the main tumor's growth and its spread. It did not, however, drive invasion in the same way. Splitting growth from invasion matters for drug aims: blocking one may not block the other. The receptor remains a clear target candidate.
plos-pone-0001116:
For many people with nerve damage, a light touch on the skin hurts. Loïs Miraucourt, Radhouane Dallel, and Daniel Voisin studied this symptom, called tactile allodynia, in a 2007 PLOS ONE article. They focused on glycine, a chemical that normally calms signals in the spinal cord.

Their work links the pain to a failure of that calming system. When glycine-based inhibition breaks down, touch signals reach a set of spinal cord cells known as PKCgamma interneurons and get read as pain. Pinpointing this route matters because allodynia is common, hard to treat, and lacks good therapies.
plos-pone-0001216:
The season in which a person is born has been linked to traits such as novelty seeking and sensation seeking. Dan Eisenberg and colleagues tested whether that link runs through dopamine genes, in a 2007 PLOS ONE article. Similar traits have also been linked with variants in dopamine receptor genes, which help the brain respond to the reward chemical dopamine.

The authors looked at season of birth and dopamine receptor gene links together, against impulsivity, sensation seeking, and reproductive behaviors. The two may combine, each shifting the other's effect. The study sits at the junction of environment, genes, and personality.
plos-pone-0001316:
Candida albicans is a fungus that lives on human surfaces without harm but can cause inflammation when it turns pathogenic. Eric Haas-Stapleton and colleagues report a striking ability of this fungus in a 2007 PLOS ONE article. Resolvins are anti-inflammatory lipids, derived from omega-3 fatty acids, that help calm neutrophil-driven inflammation.

The authors show that Candida albicans modulates host defense by biosynthesizing the pro-resolving mediator resolvin E1. This fungus making the body's own peace signal could dampen the attack against it. The finding changes how this common fungus is thought to work with immunity.
plos-pone-0001416:
Rico Tabor and Rainer Friedrich wrote a 2008 PLOS ONE study on smell circuits in the zebrafish brain. Receptors that sense the amino acid glutamate shape how smell signals are handled. Their roles had been studied in dishes, but not in the whole intact brain. The pair used drugs to probe these receptors during odor handling.

By blocking or boosting each receptor type, they mapped which ones sharpen or blur the smell pattern. The maps show how local circuits sort odors before they reach higher brain areas. That sorting is a core step in how animals tell one scent from the next. The work grounds circuit theory in a living, smelling brain.
plos-pone-0001516:
Stijn De Langhe and co-authors wrote a 2008 PLOS ONE study on lung growth and a key signal. The signal, run through a protein called beta catenin, helps form many body lineages. Its role in lung tissue lineages was vague. The team switched the signal off in the early lung tissue of mouse embryos.

Loss of the signal threw the forming of lung cell types off course. More than one lineage was hit at once. That breadth shows the signal acts as a master switch in the young lung. The work helps frame birth defects of the lung and may guide lung repair studies.
plos-pone-0001616:
Jyothi Mallajosyula and co-authors published a 2008 PLOS ONE study on an enzyme and Parkinson's disease. Levels of this enzyme, MAO-B, rise in the brain with age. That rise may add to the nerve loss of Parkinson's. A drug that blocks it is a long used therapy, paired with the standard dopamine drug. The team raised the enzyme in mouse brain support cells.

Mice with more of the enzyme in those cells grew Parkinson's like harm. That is direct proof the rise is not a mere side mark of age. It firms the case for blocker drugs. It also flags support cells as actors in the disease, not just stage hands.
plos-pone-0001716:
Carmelo Mario Vicario, Patrizia Pecoraro, Patrizia Turriziani, and their co-authors tested how space warps felt time in a 2008 PLOS ONE research article. Time, space, and numbers are linked in the physical world and, it seems, in the mind. The authors borrowed a relativity metaphor: just as motion bends time in physics, position and size may bend duration judgments in perception.

They asked whether judging how long digits stayed on screen is biased by where the digits appeared, left or right, and by their magnitude. The full text gives the timing tasks and the bias patterns. Such biases show that the brain's clock is not a neutral stopwatch. That point matters for models of timing and for tests used in brain disorders.
plos-pone-0001816:
Chad J. Creighton analyzed gene activity patterns in prostate tumors in a 2008 PLOS ONE research article. Gene transcription patterns linked to activation of oncogenes had been generated in experimental models. The oncogenes include Myc, c-Src, beta-catenin, E2F3, H-Ras, and HER2, and patterns also covered the cell cycle and androgen signaling.

Creighton asked whether these pathway signatures show coordinate expression patterns in human prostate tumors: whether pathways turn on together in real patients. The full text gives the tumor data sets and the signature correlations. Coordinated pathways suggest combination drug strategies, since blocking one route may leave its partners still driving the tumor.
plos-pone-0001916:
Gerard van der Krogt and co-authors fine-tuned a glowing sensor for a key cell signal, in a 2008 PLOS ONE study. The sensor tracks cAMP, a messenger inside cells, and glows in a way that shifts with cAMP level. It is built from a protein called Epac joined to two glowing tags, one that gives light and one that takes it.

The method, called FRET, reads the shift in glow as a live measure. The team compared pairs of glowing tags to find the pair that gives the clearest signal. A better sensor lets labs watch signals rise and fall in real time inside living cells.
plos-pone-0002016:
Satyaprakash Nayak and co-authors tested a theory of robust design against cancer data, in a 2008 PLOS ONE study. Living systems are robust: they keep working when conditions shift. The flip side, fragility, means a small nudge can cause total failure. A theory called highly optimized tolerance says systems tuned hard for one setting hide such fragile points.

The team tested that theory on the cell cycle, the steps by which cells divide. They report that fragile cell-cycle steps match the targets hit in clinical cancer trials. If fragility maps to drug targets, the theory could help pick the next targets on purpose.
plos-pone-0002116:
Jerome Casas, Thomas Steinmann, and Olivier Dangles measured the air stirred up by running spiders, in a 2008 PLOS ONE study. Many predators hunt in two modes: lying in ambush, or cruising in search of prey. Those modes have classically been studied for their energy costs, mechanics, and ecology, without weighing the signals a predator gives off and prey can perceive.

Wolf spiders run as they hunt, and their motion pushes air in a pattern prey hairs can feel. The team charted that aerodynamic signature. If prey can read the airflow, a running hunter betrays itself, and stealth becomes part of the hunting equation.
plos-pone-0002216:
Dominique Berrebi and co-authors searched for markers that flag the most dangerous kidney tumors of childhood, in a 2008 PLOS ONE paper. Nephroblastoma, also called Wilms tumor, varies widely: some cases stay local while others spread far. Cell cycle markers offered a possible way to tell them apart in advance.

The team measured cyclin E, a protein that pushes cells through division, and Ki-67, a marker of cell growth, in tumor samples. High cyclin E staining in tumor cells tracked with more aggressive disease. A marker like this could help doctors pick which children need stronger treatment from the start.
plos-pone-0002316:
Anna Linderholm, Helena Malmström, Kerstin Lidén, and co-authors warned about hidden contamination in ancient DNA samples, in a 2008 PLOS ONE paper. Ancient human DNA has been handled cautiously since problems with it surfaced in the early 1990s. Yet sequence data from old specimens underpin many studies of evolution and past ecology, so interest keeps growing.

The authors describe cryptic contamination, modern DNA that slips in without obvious signs. It can quietly lead to phylogenetic nonsense, family trees built on false sequences. Their cautions help labs tell genuine ancient results from artifacts, a basic hygiene issue for a field that reads history from bones.
plos-pone-0002416:
Led by Rappoport, a team of researchers published its study in PLOS ONE in 2008. The author list runs from Joshua Z. Rappoport, Katherine P. Heyman, Shahrnaz Kemal, and others. Its subject is dynamics of Dynamin during Clathrin Mediated Endocytosis in PC12 Cells. Members of the dynamin super-family of GTPases are involved in disparate cellular pathways.

Dynamin1 and dynamin2 have been implicated in clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Each part of the study builds on the part before it, in the order the team carried it out. In short, the piece gives a clear, short route into a field that can seem hard to enter from the outside.
plos-pone-0002516:
Research by Ancuta and co-authors came out in PLOS ONE in 2008. The author list runs from Petronela Ancuta, Anupa Kamat, Kevin J. Kunstman, and others. Its subject is microbial Translocation Is Associated with Increased Monocyte Activation and Dementia in AIDS Patients. Elevated plasma lipopolysaccharide (LPS), an indicator of microbial translocation from the gut, is a likely cause of systemic immune activation in chronic HIV infection.

What the team did, and why they did it that way, forms the core of the piece. For science readers, it shows how a small, well framed question can add a firm piece of knowledge to a much larger field.
plos-pone-0002616:
Graham and colleagues set out their study in a 2008 PLOS ONE article. The author list runs from Laurie A. Graham, Stephen C. Lougheed, K. Vanya Ewart, and others. Its subject is lateral Transfer of a Lectin-Like Antifreeze Protein Gene in Fishes.

The scattered distribution of five highly diverse AFP types across phylogenetically disparate fish species is puzzling. Each part of the study builds on the part before it, in the order the team carried it out. Readers finish with a clear sense of the problem, the approach, and why the question was worth the team's time. PLOS ONE is an open journal, and the full text can be read free by anyone who wants to check the work.
plos-pone-0002716:
Work by Joshua K. Hartshorne and colleagues appeared in PLOS ONE in 2008, dealing with visual working memory capacity and proactive interference. The catalog record names Joshua K. Hartshorne first among the authors, and the source is the open journal PLOS ONE.

The opening of the abstract sets out the basis for the work. Visual working memory capacity is extremely limited and appears to be relatively immune to practice effects or the use of explicit strategies. For readers, the value lies in how plainly the abstract sets out the problem and what the authors set out to test or describe.
plos-pone-0002816:
Work by Christine F. Skibola and colleagues appeared in PLOS ONE in 2008. Their subject was polymorphisms in the estrogen receptor 1 and vitamin c and matrix metalloproteinase gene families are associated with susceptibility to lymphoma. Authorship is credited in the record to Christine F. Skibola and co-authors, with PLOS ONE as the journal of publication.

The opening of the abstract sets out the basis for the work. Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) is the fifth most common cancer in the U.S. The authors add a further point. And few causes have been identified. Its abstract frames the work for later readers, who can judge the full text against the aims stated at the start.
plos-pone-0002916:
Elias Gounaris, Ching Tung, Clifford Restaino and colleagues imaged inflammation and polyp growth in living tissue in 2008. Up to 30 percent of polyps found in patients may shrink on their own. Judging whether a cancer therapy works needs a readout of such regression, which is hard to get.

Their method uses a light-based probe switched on by cysteine-cathepsin enzymes, which are active at sites of inflammation. Live imaging then reveals focal inflammation, new vessel growth, and polyp change over time. Published in PLOS ONE, the approach lets researchers watch disease sites respond without cutting tissue out.
plos-pone-0003016:
Qing-Peng Kong, Antonio Salas, Chang Sun and co-authors tackled fake recombinants in mitochondrial DNA datasets in 2008. Large sequencing projects handle many fragments from different genomes, creating a high risk of sample mix-ups in the lab. For genetic markers, such confusion can fabricate artificial recombinant sequences.

Writing in PLOS ONE, the team offers a way to distill, or filter out, artificial recombinants from large sets of complete mitochondrial genomes. Clean data matter because mitochondrial trees underpin studies of human origins and disease. The method helps curators spot lab-made chimeras before they mislead analysis. The article appeared in PLOS ONE, an open access journal anyone can read free online.
plos-pone-0003116:
Else Marie Agger, Ida Rosenkrands, Jon Hansen and co-authors tested a liposome adjuvant called CAF01 in 2008. For vaccines against influenza, malaria, and HIV, antibody responses alone are not enough; a strong cell-based response is also needed for enough protection. Some diseases need still other response types, so one adjuvant rarely fits all.

CAF01 pairs cationic liposomes with a synthetic form of mycobacterial cord factor. The team presents it as a versatile adjuvant for vaccines with different immune needs. Published in PLOS ONE, such range in an adjuvant would make vaccine design simpler across diseases. Readers can follow the full methods and data in the complete text of the article.
plos-pone-0003216:
Reginia H. Y. Yan, Jessica L. Malisch, Robert M. Hannon and colleagues test a famous finger ratio claim in mice in this 2008 PLOS ONE paper. The ratio of second digit length to fourth digit length tends to be lower in men than in women. This 2D:4D ratio is often used as a proxy for prenatal androgen exposure in studies of human health and behaviour.

By selective breeding for a behavioural trait, the team show digit ratio itself can change. Readers learn that the ratio is not a fixed fossil of hormone exposure alone. The result urges caution when finger measures are used to explain human behaviour.
plos-pone-0003316:
Zhi-Hua Chen and co-authors link a stress gene to cell cleanup in damaged lungs in this 2008 PLOS ONE paper. COPD is a lung disease that gets worse over time. Cigarette smoke drives odd cell responses that break down lung tissue and narrow air flow. Autophagy, where cells digest their own worn parts in lysosomes, is part of that response.

The title reports the gene Egr-1 controls autophagy in smoke-induced COPD. Readers see a stress switch tied to a cleanup path that can help or harm, in excess. Tuning that path may be one way to slow smoke damage in lungs.
plos-pone-0003416:
Guadalupe Gómez-Baena and co-authors studied sugar use by an ocean microbe in this 2008 paper. Prochlorococcus is a tiny sea bacterium that lives by photosynthesis. It was long treated as feeding on sunlight and air alone. No one had directly tested whether it can take up sugars.

The team used strains adapted to bright light and to dim light. Both could take up glucose from the water around them. Glucose also changed which genes the cells switched on. The result blurs the line between pure plant-like feeding and a more mixed diet.
plos-pone-0003516:
Shen Yin and co-authors studied chromosome sorting in mouse eggs for this 2008 paper. Meiosis halves chromosome counts to make eggs and sperm. Partner chromosomes part in the first division, sister copies in the second. Why sisters stay joined during the first round was the question.

A protein called Shugoshin1 appears to guard that join. Its role covers both partner separation and sister handling in oocytes. Losing such a guard would scramble the divisions. The work clarifies a choreography every gamete depends on. Egg errors are a leading cause of failed births in mammals.
plos-pone-0003616:
Alessandra Bandera and co-authors studied immune recovery after stem cell transplants in this 2008 paper. Autologous transplants return a patient's own blood stem cells. CD4 helper T cell counts stay low for a time afterward. Unlike in HIV, opportunistic infections stay uncommon in these patients.

The team found fully competent CD8 T lymphocytes present in recipients. Those killer cells worked despite an ineffectual T-helper response. Working killers may explain the missing infections. The result separates cell counts from true immune function. Stem cell grafts are now standard care for many blood cancers.
plos-pone-0003716:
Chun-Hong Zhu, Jinyong Kim, Jerry W. Shay, and colleagues published this cell study in PLOS ONE in 2008. When cells are stressed, they park stalled protein-making machinery in blobs called stress granules. A screen for genes that protect human muscle cells from oxidative stress turned up a new protein, SGNP.

SGNP sits in both stress granules and the nucleolus, the cell's ribosome factory. The evidence ties it to the handling and transport of 5.8S ribosomal RNA. The finding links the cell's emergency depots with the making of its protein factories, two systems usually studied apart.
plos-pone-0003816:
Ha Tran, Huaiyang Chen, Andreas Walz, and colleagues published this smell study in PLOS ONE in 2008. In the olfactory bulb, the brain's first relay for smell, sensory axons meet the dendrites of mitral and tufted cells in set patterns. How those dendrites grow out was less well regulated in the literature than axon targeting.

The team found the olfactory epithelium, the smell-sensing sheet in the nose, influences that outgrowth. Its signals shape how mitral and tufted cell dendrites develop. The result shows the sensory surface talking back to the brain wiring it feeds.
plos-pone-0003916:
João Fadista, Marianne Nygaard, Lars-Erik Holm, and co-authors gave a first survey of pig genome variation in 2008. Recent work showed mammal genomes vary in how many copies of regions they carry. Those copy number variants help shape traits, health, and disease. Pigs had not yet had such a survey.

Their PLOS ONE article reports variants across parts of chromosomes 4, 7, 14, and 17. It offers a first snapshot rather than a whole-genome count. Pig breeders and researchers can build on that start. The data also aid use of pigs as models for human disease.
plos-pone-0004016:
Robert M. Suryan, David J. Anderson, Scott A. Shaffer, and co-authors linked albatross form to their ranges in 2008. Large albatrosses harvest wind and wave energy for cheap long flights. Their wing shape suits the windy oceans they patrol. Most species therefore stay in those wind belts.

Their PLOS ONE article argues that specialization may limit range expansion. Endangered albatrosses cannot easily shift as oceans warm. Wings built for strong winds perform poorly in calm zones. Conservation plans must account for that built-in limit on movement. The article came out in PLOS ONE, an open journal for science and health research.
plos-pone-0004116:
Marie-Christine Meunier, Chantal Baron, and Claude Perreault tracked cancer-fighting T cells in mice in 2009. CD8 T cells primed against minor antigens can erase leukemia and solid tumors. The H7a antigen is one such target in their model. Why these cells work so potently was not fully clear.

Their PLOS ONE article follows the injected cells inside tumor-bearing mice. Two host factors governed how long the T cells persisted. Persistence likely decides whether tumors return after early success. Knowing the factors could improve cell therapy design. The paper came out in PLOS ONE, an open journal for work in science and health.
plos-pone-0004216:
Mary Anna Carbone and colleagues published this glaucoma study in PLOS ONE in 2009. Glaucoma is the world's second leading cause of bilateral blindness, killing retinal ganglion cells over time. The protein myocilin is tied to congenital glaucoma. It is also tied to two to four percent of primary open angle glaucoma cases. But how it causes disease was unclear.

The team overproduced myocilin in the fruit fly eye. They report that this activates the unfolded protein response, the cell's alarm for misfolded proteins. The result points to protein-folding stress as the route from myocilin to eye damage.
plos-pone-0004316:
Michael Seidman and colleagues published this inflammation genetics study in PLOS ONE in 2009. Knocking out or inhibiting PECAM, an adhesion molecule on blood vessel walls, impairs inflammatory responses in several mouse strains. Yet on the C57BL/6 background, no such phenotype appears, hinting that other genes compensate.

The team studied thioglycollate peritonitis, a standard belly inflammation model, in these mice. They report a PECAM-independent form of the response associated with a locus on mouse chromosome 2. A backup inflammation route, mapped to one chromosome region, may explain why the knockout disappoints. The locus is a stretch of DNA whose exact gene is still to be named.
plos-pone-0004416:
Skin cells called keratinocytes are the storehouse at the center of a 2009 study by Lusine Danielyan, Sebastian Zellmer, Stefan Sickinger, and co-authors, published in PLOS ONE. The team mapped glutamine synthetase, an enzyme that builds the amino acid glutamine, across human and rat skin. In inner organs glutamine supports cell growth, waste removal, and strong barriers.

What was not clear was how the enzyme is spread through skin, and how that pattern changes with age and body site. The authors report that skin holds the enzyme in reserve and can switch on more of it when ammonium builds up. Their map gives skin science a clearer picture of how the body's largest organ handles nitrogen and protects itself.
plos-pone-0004516:
Cells from patients with a rare immune disorder handle copying stress badly, show Michal Schwartz, Yifat Oren, Assaf Bester, and co-authors in PLOS ONE in 2009. DNA double-strand breaks are among the worst injuries a cell can suffer. One repair system, called non-homologous end joining, also plays a key role in building immune receptors in white blood cells.

Patients with mutations in a gene of that system, Cernunnos, also called XLF, suffer immunodeficiency. The team studied how their cells respond when DNA replication is stressed. The response was impaired, as the title reports. That adds a second weakness to the known repair defect, and helps explain why these patients face both immune failure and broader health problems.
plos-pone-0004616:
Wild frogs exposed to a virus show signs of selection on an immune gene, report Amber Teacher, Trenton Garner, and Richard Nichols in PLOS ONE in 2009. The common frog, Rana temporaria, is a popular study species. Its major histocompatibility complex, a set of immune genes, had been well characterized in the laboratory frog Xenopus but not in this species, nor in wild frogs at all.

Ranavirus is a viral pathogen sweeping through wild amphibian populations. The team studied a novel MHC class I marker in frogs exposed to the virus. They found evidence for directional selection, variation being pushed in one direction by survival. Wild populations evolving under disease pressure, documented in real time, helps conservationists judge which frog stocks may resist the epidemic.
plos-pone-0004716:
Hyun-Gwan Lee, Suman Rohila, and Kyung-An Han traced how a fly receptor drives egg laying through a calcium linked enzyme, in PLOS ONE in 2009. Egg laying is vital for reproduction, yet the cell steps that drive it are poorly known. The team built on past work with a receptor for octopamine, the insect match of a human stress signal.

They showed the receptor acts in the egg duct lining through a calcium tuned enzyme. That chain links a nerve signal to the muscle like squeeze that moves eggs. The detail helps explain insect reproduction in clear steps. It may also aid pest control.
plos-pone-0004816:
Haider Warraich and colleagues measured prevalence of obesity in school going children of Karachi, in PLOS ONE in 2009. Obesity is an emerging problem in Pakistan. The authors sought to determine prevalence of obesity and malnutrition in school children from grades six to eight in different Karachi schools. Assess associations affecting weight in this urban adolescent group.

Cross sectional surveys found both over and under nutrition coexisting. Urban diets and activity patterns are shifting rapidly. School based data can target health programs. Pakistan faces a double burden requiring balanced policy. These findings offer a firm starting point for the next round of testing.
plos-pone-0004916:
Emily Cotter and colleagues assessed health and human rights education in United States schools of medicine and public health, in PLOS ONE in 2009. Despite increasing recognition of importance of human rights in protection and promotion of health. Formal human rights education has been lacking in schools of medicine and public health. Objectives were to determine nature and extent of current teaching and future challenges through surveys of programs nationwide.

Coverage is sparse and uneven across schools. Future clinicians lack rights based training. Curricular reform has clear baselines now. Health equity needs educational foundations. Replication in other settings will show how robust the findings really are.
plos-pone-0005016:
Bovine tuberculosis jumps between badgers and cattle. That cross-species spread frustrates control efforts. Monika Böhm, Michael Hutchings and Piran White mapped the contact network behind it. Their PLOS ONE paper appeared in 2009. They studied a wildlife-livestock host community. Their goal was to identify high-risk individuals.

Contact patterns show which animals meet often enough to spread disease. A few individuals may drive most transmission. Targeting those key spreaders could break the chain. That would be smarter than blanket culling. The work applies network thinking to a stubborn farming problem. It may reshape how bovine TB is managed in Britain and beyond.
plos-pone-0005116:
Male chimpanzees hunt together and share meat. Males often give meat to unrelated females. Cristina Gomes and Christophe Boesch tested the meat-for-sex hypothesis in wild chimpanzees. Their PLOS ONE paper appeared in 2009. The hypothesis says males trade meat for mating access. Short-term trades had been hard to prove.

The exchange plays out on a long-term basis. Males who shared meat with females over months mated more with them. No instant swap was needed. The finding reveals a slow economy of favors in chimp society. It resembles long-term reciprocal arrangements in humans. The study is a rare long look at wild behavior. Years of observation underlie its conclusion.
plos-pone-0005216:
Newborn mammals spend their first days in close contact with their mothers, and that contact builds bonding. Yet many routine procedures after birth separate babies from mothers for a time. Henry and colleagues studied how early handling shapes later life, reported in PLOS ONE in 2009.

Their title states the finding: neonatal handling affects bonding and social development in a lasting way. Early experience, even brief handling, left durable marks on how the young animals related to others. The work supports care practices that protect early contact where health needs allow.
plos-pone-0005316:
Hoofed animals once roamed widely across the southern Levant, the lands of Israel, Palestine, and Jordan. Humans have lived there in dense, successive cultures for about fifteen thousand years. Tsahar and colleagues traced what happened to those ungulates over that span in PLOS ONE in 2009.

The study mapped where each hoofed species lived during the Holocene and which ones vanished. Long human impact on the landscape had great ecological consequences, including local extinctions. The record offers a baseline for conservation in a region shaped by people longer than almost anywhere.
plos-pone-0005416:
HIV prevalence among state prison inmates in the United States is more than five times higher than outside prison. Yet transmission inside prisons is sparsely documented. Jafa and colleagues investigated HIV seroconversions in the Georgia prison system in PLOS ONE in 2009.

The study covered eighty-eight seroconversions reported between 1988 and 2005 among male inmates.
